multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I don't want to ___ (to disappoint / you).
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We're no strangers to grammar, you know the rules and so do I, a full commitment's what I'm thinking of, you wouldn't get this from any other deck. I just wanna tell you how I'm feeling, gotta make you understand, never gonna give you up, never gonna let you down, never gonna run around and desert you, never gonna make you cry, never gonna say goodbye, never gonna tell a lie and hurt you. Sincerely Yours, This Deck.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to rise' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO RISE - ROSE - RISEN.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Chris moved from parents when he was 18. He has lived by ___  since that time.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: By himself' means 'alone'. We cannot use any other form of a pronoun in this phrase.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This chair has a _________ cover that looks like natural.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The adjective ‘leathery’ means ‘looking or feeling like leather’: leathery skin/hands, her leathery brown skin; a leathery aroma; a leathery purse; Audri twisted her leathery old hands together in worry.; His skin is quite leathery as a result of too much sun. The synonym of ‘leathery’ is ‘leatherlike’. The adjective ‘leather’ means ‘of the skin of an animal prepared for making clothes, shoes, etc.’: a leather coat/belt/handbag/seat; leather boots, a leather sofa, a leather jacket. The words ‘leatherish’ and ‘leatheric’ are nonce-words. In the test sentence ‘This chair has a _________ cover that looks like natural.’ we see the key-words ‘that looks like natural’. Thus, we are to choose ANSWER 4 (leathery).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___, Mark's team was beaten in the semi-final.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or the place (where, when, how, how often, etc.) Many adverbs are formed from adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I visited a cousin ___ is a dentist.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'that' and 'who' for people in relative clauses. 'Whose' and 'whom' are used as objects.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Do you know any means of protection ___ radiation?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'protection from'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I like travelling ___ sea.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'to travel by sea'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I'm worried ___ my exams.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'worried about'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I've seen three ___ (a deer) in the forest today.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are some nouns which have the same form in the singular and in the plural: ONE DEER - TWO DEER.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I've heard ___. I think we are not alone in the house.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the pronoun 'something' to refer to things in affirmative sentences, while 'anything' in negative ones. 'Any' and 'some' are pronouns which don't relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If I __________ (to be) you I ____________ (not to swim) in cold water.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about imaginary situations which differ from real facts in the present we use Conditional 2: If-clause (if + Past Simple) - Main Clause (would/could + present without 'to'). The meaning of this sentence: in reality you swim in cold water so I recommend you not to do it.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: "Tiffany: ""I'll go to the GYM tomorrow""."
options: Tiffany said that she had gone to the GYM the next day.
Tiffany said that she went to the GYM tomorrow.
Tiffany said that she would go to the GYM tomorrow.
Tiffany said that she would go to the GYM the next day.

options_map.A: Tiffany said that she had gone to the GYM the next day.
options_map.B: Tiffany said that she went to the GYM tomorrow.
options_map.C: Tiffany said that she would go to the GYM tomorrow.
options_map.D: Tiffany said that she would go to the GYM the next day.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Tiffany said that she would go to the GYM the next day.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We change the Future Simple to the Conditional in Reported Speech: will - would. Also we change time expressions: tomorrow - the next day.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Single out the string with the right word order:
options: John was wearing a fantastic Italian coat.
John was wearing an Italian fantastic coat.
John was a fantastic Italian coat wearing.
John was an Italian fantastic coat wearing.

options_map.A: John was wearing a fantastic Italian coat.
options_map.B: John was wearing an Italian fantastic coat.
options_map.C: John was a fantastic Italian coat wearing.
options_map.D: John was an Italian fantastic coat wearing.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: John was wearing a fantastic Italian coat.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There is a certain word order in statements with the Past Continuous Tense: Subject - Auxiliary - Predicate with -ing ending - Object. When we need to use many adjectives in one sentence, they should be placed in the following order: Opinion - Size - Age - Shape - Colour - Origin - Material. 'Fantastic' is an opinion adjective and 'Italian' is an adjective of origin.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My brother wants to become ___ policeman.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use articles 'a/an' when we talk about jobs.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I was going to a supermarket when the fire _____________ (to break) out.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: In this case the first action was in progress when suddenly something interrupted it. For a longer action we use the Past Continuous Tense. The second action was shorter so we should use the Past Simple Tense.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Well, I ___ (to take) this pair of shoes.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Simple Tense when we have no plan or decision before we speak. We make it at the time of speaking.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: New Year ___ (to celebrate) all over the world.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we don't know who carries out the action, or it is obvious or unimportant to us, we use the Passive voice. The Passive is formed: BE + Past Participle.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My car is too dirty. I ___ clean it immediately.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the modal verb 'must' when we talk about duties or when it is necessary to do something.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I hate this town. I will never ___ (to return) here again.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verbs are verbs that consist of a verb and a particle and/or a preposition. Phrasal verbs are typical of spoken English or informal writing, e.g. letters to friends and articles in popular journalism. They cannot be understood based upon the meanings of the individual parts in isolation, thus, their meanings are unpredictable. The phrasal verb 'to go back' means 'to return'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If someone comes tell ___ to wait for a while.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Cambridge and Oxford grammarians say that we often use the plural pronouns ‘they’, ‘them’, ‘their’ etc., to refer back to (singular) someone or somebody when we do not know if the person is male or female, despite the fact that they are referring back to a singular noun: Never judge someone by the way they look.; A researcher has to be completely objective in their findings.; Someone has forgotten their handbag. Or we can say ‘Never judge someone by the way he or she looks.’; A researcher has to be completely objective in his or her findings.; Someone has forgotten his or her handbag. Some people object to the use of plural pronouns in this type of situation on the grounds that it’s ungrammatical. In fact, the use of plural pronouns to refer back to a singular subject isn’t new - it dates back to the 16 th century and now it’s common in current English and it is now widely accepted. The American Heritage College Dictionary’ recommends to use ‘he or she’ when you are writing a formal document.In the test sentence ‘If someone comes tell ______ to wait for a while.’ that is the example of the oral speech we need to choose the pronoun that is the object of the sentence: ‘…tell (whom?) ______ to wait…’. Therefore, we need to choose ANSWER 4 (them).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Monkey is ___ animal I've ever seen.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we compare a person or a thing with more than one person or one thing we use the superlative form of adjectives. If we use a two-syllable adjective ending in -y, -w, -ly we add '-est' to it.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___, he managed to do it.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or the place (where, when, how, how often, etc.) Many adverbs are formed from adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The person ______ I phoned 2 days ago is my grandfather.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: What' is a question word, it cannot be used here. We use 'which' for animals and objects. 'Whose' refers to possession and 'whom' is used as an object.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jack has got some reasons ___ moving to London.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'reason for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We have no information about where he is but ___ least we know where he planned to go.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'at least'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I was astonished _____ her performance.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'astonished by'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Every human has got 32 _______ (a tooth).
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The noun 'tooth' has the irregular plural form: TOOTH - TEETH

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We didn't have ___ success with that task.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 'Much' is used before uncountable nouns. 'Many' and 'a few' - before countable. We use 'some' in positive sentences.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If he _______ (to be) at home we _________ (to tell) him everything.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about probable situations in the present or future we use Conditional 1: If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future/modal + present without 'to') or If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future + HAVE TO, OUGHT TO, BE TO + present without 'to')

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Sister: ''Don't put this T-shirt on".
options: Sister asked me did not to put this T-shirt on.
Sister asked me did not put this T-shirt on.
Sister asked me not to put this T-shirt on.
Sister asked me to put this T-shirt not on.

options_map.B: Sister asked me did not put this T-shirt on.
options_map.C: Sister asked me not to put this T-shirt on.
options_map.D: Sister asked me to put this T-shirt not on.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Sister asked me not to put this T-shirt on.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we need to transform a request into Reported Speech we use an introductory verb + the to-infinitive: asked not + to put.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Single out the string with the right word order
options: They not are walking in the park.
They are walking in the park not.
Not they are walking in the park.
They are not walking in the park.

options_map.A: They not are walking in the park.
options_map.B: They are walking in the park not.
options_map.C: Not they are walking in the park.
options_map.D: They are not walking in the park.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: They are not walking in the park.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To make a negative sentence in the Present Continuous Tense we put the subject and the auxiliary verb 'are' in the first place. The negative particle 'not' is always after the auxiliary verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Simon is very busy. He _________ (to take) a rest very seldom.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we talk about things in general, permanent situations and states or things that happen sometimes, we always use the Present Simple Tense: [I/you/we/they/ + Verb] and [he/she/it + Verb+ -s(es)].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Bill ________________ (to play) football at 10 o'clock yesterday.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Past Continuous Tense when we talk about an action which was in progress at a certain time in the past and if we don't mention when it was started or finished.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I have won the lottery. I ___ (to donate) the prize to charity. I had decided to do that before.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use ‘be going to’ when we have already made a plan or an arrangement, or we have intentions: I am going to fly to Vienna tomorrow.; They are going to Montenegro on holidays in August.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: "Opera ""Rigoletto"" ___ (to compose) by Giuseppe Verdi in 1851."
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Sometimes we need to change a sentence from the Active Voice into the Passive Voice. We can also know a person who carries out the action. In this case we use the Passive Voice and form a sentence according to this rule:  Subject - Be+ Past Participle - Preposition 'BY' - Agent (who or what carries out the action). In this sentence the action took place at a certain time in the past, so we use the Past Simple Passive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: He is a good sportsman, but he ___ stop smoking.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the modal verb 'should' when we give advice or recommend something.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I think it's important  ___ (to stay in good relationships) with your colleagues.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verbs are verbs that consist of a verb and a particle and/or a preposition. Phrasal verbs are typical of spoken English or informal writing, e.g. letters to friends and articles in popular journalism. They cannot be understood based upon the meanings of the individual parts in isolation, thus, their meanings are unpredictable. The phrasal verb 'to keep in' means 'to stay in good relationships with somebody'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to see' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO SEE - SAW - SEEN.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We've bought a boat for ___ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When the same person is both the subject and the object in the sentence we use a reflexive pronoun after a verb or a preposition. 'Ourselves' is the right reflexive form of the personal pronoun 'We'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This black dress is _______ than the blue one.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we compare two things or two people we use the comparative form of adjectives. If we use an adjective with three or more syllables we add 'more' before it.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Susan plays the piano ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or the place (where, when, how, how often, etc.) Many adverbs are formed from adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Tom asked me about Mary, ___ travelled with us last summer.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'who' for people in relative clauses when 'who' is a subject. 'Whose' and 'whom' are used as objects. We use 'which' to refer to animals and objects.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: He doesn't have any respect ___ his relatives.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'respect for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Kate is always ___ the phone talking about everything in the world.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'on the phone'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jeremy is very unfriendly ___ Kate.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: For this sentence we need to choose a preposition after the adjective ‘unfriendly’ that means ‘showing dislike and no sympathy’. We can use three prepositions after the adjective ‘unfriendly’: (1) ‘to’ (The Jacobs have always been very unfriendly to us.), (2) ‘towards’ (Why is she suddenly so unfriendly towards you, Charlie?) and (3) ‘with’ (Why are you so unfriendly with Polina?). Therefore, among the test variants we choose ANSWER 4 (to).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I watched two ___ (a series) of ""Friends"" yesterday.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are some nouns which have the same form in the singular and in the plural: ONE SERIES - TWO SERIES.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: There are ___ cats on the bench.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Many' is used before countable nouns. 'Much' and 'a little' - before uncountable. We use 'any' in negative sentences.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If I ___ (to be) an actor I ___ (to choose) roles in action movies.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about imaginary situations which differ from real facts in the present we use Conditional 2: If-clause (if + Past Simple) - Main Clause (would/could + present without 'to'). The meaning of this sentence: in reality I'm not an actor.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: "Mary: ""I usually leave home at 9 o'clock""."
options: Mary said that she would usually leave home at 9 o'clock.
Mary said that she was usually leaving home at 9 o'clock.
Mary said that she had usually left home at 9 o'clock.
Mary said that she usually left home at 9 o'clock.

options_map.A: Mary said that she would usually leave home at 9 o'clock.
options_map.B: Mary said that she was usually leaving home at 9 o'clock.
options_map.C: Mary said that she had usually left home at 9 o'clock.
options_map.D: Mary said that she usually left home at 9 o'clock.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Mary said that she usually left home at 9 o'clock.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We change the Present Simple to the Past Simple in Reported Speech.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Single out the option with the right word order?
options: New Zealand is about the same size as Great Britain or Japan.
New Zealand about the same size as Great Britain or Japan is.
About the same size as Great Britain or Japan New Zealand is.
New Zealand about the same size is as Great Britain or Japan.

options_map.A: New Zealand is about the same size as Great Britain or Japan.
options_map.B: New Zealand about the same size as Great Britain or Japan is.
options_map.C: About the same size as Great Britain or Japan New Zealand is.
options_map.D: New Zealand about the same size is as Great Britain or Japan.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: New Zealand is about the same size as Great Britain or Japan.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There is a certain word order in statements with the Present Simple Tense: Subject - Auxiliary - Object. 'New Zealand' is a subject, 'is' - an auxiliary verb, ' about the same size as Great Britain or Japan' - an object.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: He wrote a poem for her. ___ poem was beautiful.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'the' with all kinds of nouns when we talk about definite and specific things. 'The' also goes before nouns mentioned for the second time.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It ___ (to get) colder. Do you really want to go out?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: In this sentence we are talking about temporary situation. Also we know that the action is happening at this certain moment. So, in this case we should always use the Present Continuous Tense. This Tense is formed: am/is/are + Verb-ing. With ing-ending the verb 'get' should be spelled with double 't'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Henry ___ (to talk) to his cousin while his wife was reading a newspaper.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Past Continuous Tense when we talk about two or more simultaneous actions in the past.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: He has to do so much today. He _____________ (to be) tired after work.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Simple Tense when we talk about common actions and facts which will happen in the future.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This single ___ (to release) last month.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we don't know who carries out the action, or it is obvious or unimportant to us, we use the Passive voice. The Passive is formed: BE + Past Participle.  In this sentence the action took place at a certain time in the past, so we use the Past Simple Passive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It's very cold outside. We ___ put on warm clothes.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the modal verb 'have to' when it is not our idea to do something, when we are forced to do something by somebody or by circumstances.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I need ___ (to complete) this project until the end of this month.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verbs are verbs that consist of a verb and a particle and/or a preposition. Phrasal verbs are typical of spoken English or informal writing, e.g. letters to friends and articles in popular journalism. They cannot be understood based upon the meanings of the individual parts in isolation, thus, their meanings are unpredictable. The phrasal verb 'to carry out' means 'to complete something'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to sing' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO SING - SANG - SUNG.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jill didn't answer Martin. She didn't know what to tell ______ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Here the pronoun should be used in its objective form. 'him' is the right form of the personal pronoun 'he'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The service is currently ___ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that the adjective 'available' is used with the prefix 'un-'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Nick spoke ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or the place (where, when, how, how often, etc.) Many adverbs are formed from adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jack took the pen, ___ was red.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'which' or 'that' for things in relative clauses. 'Whose' and 'whom' are used as objects.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My brother is a great specialist ____ IT.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'specialist in'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: They invited us ___ dinner.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'for dinner'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Who is responsible ___ this mess?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'responsible for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My grandma has several _________ (a swine) in the village.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are some nouns which have the same form in the singular and in the plural: ONE SWINE - TWO SWINE

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We've seen ___ animals in the zoo today.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: A lot of' is used before uncountable and countable nouns in positive sentences. 'Much' and 'a little' - before uncountable. We use 'any' in negative sentences.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If you ___ (to drive) so slowly we ___ (to be) late.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about probable situations in the present or future we use Conditional 1: If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future/modal + present without 'to') or If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future + HAVE TO, OUGHT TO, BE TO + present without 'to').

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: "Tom: "Will you go there with me?"
options: Tom asked me I would go there with him.
Tom asked me if I would go there with him.
Tom asked me if would I go there with him.
Tom asked me if I went there with him.

options_map.A: Tom asked me I would go there with him.
options_map.B: Tom asked me if I would go there with him.
options_map.C: Tom asked me if would I go there with him.
options_map.D: Tom asked me if I went there with him.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Tom asked me if I would go there with him.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Tom asked me if I would go there with him.' - this is the right word order in Reported Speech for general questions. We add 'if' before a pronoun and then place an auxiliary.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Single out the option with the right word order:
options: You have ever been to London?
Have you ever been to London?
Have you been ever to London?
Have you been to London ever ?

options_map.A: You have ever been to London?
options_map.B: Have you ever been to London?
options_map.C: Have you been ever to London?
options_map.D: Have you been to London ever ?

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Have you ever been to London?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To make a question in the Present Perfect Tense we put the auxiliary verb 'have' in the first place. Then comes the subject, the adverb, the verb, and the phrase of place. We should always put the adverb between two verbs - auxiliary and the verb in the Past Participle.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We travelled to ___ Netherlands last year.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: No article is used when we refer to a country with a single name (except The Gambia) or with merged single-named states Bosnia and Herzegovina: Japan, Mongolia, Canada, France, Egypt, etc. We use ‘the’ before countries (1) with plural names (the Philippines, the Maldives, the Netherlands); (2) with names containing a noun stating the kind of state (the Republic, the Democratic, the State(s), the Union, the Confederation, the Kingdom, the Commonwealth, the Principality). Therefore, we are to choose ANSWER 3 (the).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I ___ (to know) Alex since 1999.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The action in this sentence started in the Past (1999) and continues in the Present. It means that I still know Alex. In this case we should use the Present Perfect Tense:  has/have + Verb (-ed/Past Participle).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Paul ___ (to read) the first book when he was four years old.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Past Simple Tense when we talk about actions which happened at a certain time in the past.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Carol ___ (to be) busy tomorrow.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Simple Tense when we talk about common actions and facts which will happen in the future.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The door ___ (to break) 2 hours ago.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we don't know who carries out the action, or it is obvious or unimportant to us, we use the Passive voice. The Passive is formed: BE + Past Participle. In this sentence the action took place at a certain time in the past, so we use the Past Simple Passive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I can't hear you at all. ___ you speak louder?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the modal verb 'could' when we ask somebody to do something.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jennifer, could you  ___ (to take care of somebody) my cat for a couple of days?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verbs are verbs that consist of a verb and a particle and/or a preposition. Phrasal verbs are typical of spoken English or informal writing, e.g. letters to friends and articles in popular journalism. They cannot be understood based upon the meanings of the individual parts in isolation, thus, their meanings are unpredictable. The phrasal verb 'to look after' means 'to take care of somebody'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to speak' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO SPEAK - SPOKE - SPOKEN.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: He went to the shop but he bought ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Everything' and 'something' do not relate to the meaning of the sentence. 'Anything' is used in negative sentences. As an alternative we could use 'not anything': 'But he did not buy anything'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Dave took some pictures of wonderful ___ clouds.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The words ‘featherly’ and ‘featheric’ are nonce-words.The adjective ‘feathery’ means ‘soft or delicate, or made of many very small and delicate pieces’: feathery clouds/leaves, feathery blond hair. The synonyms of ‘feathery’ are ‘soft’ and ‘fluffy’.The noun ‘feather’ means ‘one of the many soft, light things that cover a bird’s body, consisting of along, thin, central part with material like hairs along each side’: feather pillows (= containing feathers).In the test sentence ‘Dave took some pictures of wonderful _________ clouds.’ we need to choose the adjective that describes clouds.Thus, we are to choose ANSWER 3 (feathery).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Sandy was dancing ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or the place (where, when, how, how often, etc.) Many adverbs are formed from adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Michael has bought a suit ___ is black.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'which' or 'that' for things in relative clauses. 'Whose' and 'whom' are used as objects.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jane has a talent ___ playing the piano.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'talent for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jim and Sandra walked in silence _____ a while.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'for a while'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I'm interested ______ science.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'interested in'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Have you already heard this ___ ?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Some nouns are always plural: SCISSORS / GLASSES / TROUSERS / JEANS / SHORTS / TIGHTS / PYJAMAS / NEWS etc.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I don't want to take ________ luggage with me.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'some' in positive sentences and 'any' in negative ones before countable or uncountable nouns. 'Many' and 'a few' are used before plural countable nouns

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If I ___ (to have) one billion dollars I ___ (to donate) a half to charity.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The second conditional is used to talk about unreal, unlikely, impossible or imaginary things, events or situations. The structure is usually if + past simple (the hypothetical or unlikely part) and would/could/might + infinitive (the possible result of the imaginary situation). As the test answers consist only of ‘had/donated’ and ‘would have/would donate’ variants, the test sentence ‘If I ________ (to have) one billion dollars I ________ (to donate) a half to charity.’ describes an unlikely situation. It means that ‘I don’t have one billion dollars, that is why I can’t donate a half to charity.’ The speaker is still thinking about the future possibility, but it is imaginary – I imagine that I could donate some money to charity, but it is unlikely. In this case the question between the first and the second conditional is often a question of the speaker’s attitude to the situation.As for the test ANSWER, we are to choose ANSWER 2 (had/would donate).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Stephanie: "I'm doing my homework now".
options: Stephanie said that she was doing her homework now.
Stephanie said that she had been doing her homework then.
Stephanie said that she was doing her homework then.
Stephanie said that she had been doing her homework now.

options_map.A: Stephanie said that she was doing her homework now.
options_map.B: Stephanie said that she had been doing her homework then.
options_map.C: Stephanie said that she was doing her homework then.
options_map.D: Stephanie said that she had been doing her homework now.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Stephanie said that she was doing her homework then.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We change the Present Continuous to the Past Continuous in Reported Speech. Also we change some time expressions: now - then.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Single out the option with the right word order
options: Bad Bellingen is a nice small town in Germany.
Bad Bellingen is a small nice town in Germany.
In Germany Bad Bellingen is a nice small town.
In Germany Bad Bellingen is a small nice town.

options_map.A: Bad Bellingen is a nice small town in Germany.
options_map.B: Bad Bellingen is a small nice town in Germany.
options_map.C: In Germany Bad Bellingen is a nice small town.
options_map.D: In Germany Bad Bellingen is a small nice town.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Bad Bellingen is a nice small town in Germany.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There is a certain word order in statements with the Present Simple Tense: Subject - Auxiliary - Object. When we need to use many adjectives in one sentence, they should be placed in the following order: Opinion - Size - Age - Shape - Colour - Origin - Material. 'Nice' is an opinion adjective and 'small' refers to size.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I ate ___ plum and went out.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the article 'a' with singular countable nouns also to show the quantity - only one.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I like to watch thrillers, but now I ___ (to watch) a comedy.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The adverb 'now' means that the action is happening at this certain moment. So, in this case we should always use the Present Continuous Tense. This Tense is formed: Auxiliary (am/is/are) + Verb-ing.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: First of all, we visited the British Museum, then we went to Hyde Park and last we ___ (to relax) in a restaurant.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the past tense to talk about something that happened once in the past - a completed action in a time before now. Duration is not important: Sally watched TV last night.; Did you play tennis at weekends?. It can also be used for actions taking place one after another or in the middle of another action: She entered a cafe, took off her coat, sat down and took the menu.; Roby fell off the tree and her friends took her to a doctor.In the test sentence ‘First of all, we visited the British Museum, then we went to Hyde Park and last we______ (to relax) in a restaurant.’. we need to form the past form of the regular verb ‘relax’. For regular verbs, we add -ed to the base form of the verb (work – worked) or -d if the verb already ends in e (move – moved). Therefore, we are to choose ANSWER 2 (relaxed).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Ok, I’ve decided! I ___ (to go) to the gallery tomorrow.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Simple Tense when we talk about common actions and facts which will happen in the future. We can use the Future Simple (will and shall) to express immediate intentions and decisions: Will you come for dinner on Saturday? If we chose ANSWER 3 (will go), it will sound like the speaker’s immediate decision.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This work ___ (to complete) tomorrow.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we don't know who carries out the action, or it is obvious or unimportant to us, we use the Passive voice. In this sentence we speak about the action which will be completed in the future: Will Be + Past Participle.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Susan is 10 and she ______________ skate yet.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The modal verb 'can' is used when we speak about the ability in the Present.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Rachel is ___ (to stay in anticipation) summer holiday.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verbs are verbs that consist of a verb and a particle and/or a preposition. Phrasal verbs are typical of spoken English or informal writing, e.g. letters to friends and articles in popular journalism. They cannot be understood based upon the meanings of the individual parts in isolation, thus, their meanings are unpredictable. The phrasal verb 'to look forward to' means 'to stay in anticipation'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to steal' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO STEAL - STOLE - STOLEN.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Nicki left Peter and returned to Seattle. Now she lives by ___ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: By herself' means 'alone'. We cannot use any other form of a pronoun in this phrase.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Chris found a ________ ________ _________ (cute/little/grey) kitten.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is very unusual to have more than three adjectives in front of a noun. But if it is so, the most usual sequence of adjectives is the following: 1. general opinion (good, bad, lovely, strange, nice, important,etc.), 2. specific opinion (a) food: tasty; delicious; (b) furniture, buildings: comfortable; uncomfortable;(c) people, animals: clever; friendly), 3. size (big, tall), 4. physical quality (thin, rough, untidy), 5. shape (round, square), 6. age (old, babyish), 7. colour (green, pastel), 8. origin (Japanese, northern), 9. material(metal, wood, plastic), 10. type (general-purpose, U-shaped, bedroom, four-sided), 11. purpose (folding, swinging, work, racing).Therefore, in the test sentence ‘Chris found a _______ _______ ________ (cute/little/grey) kitten.’ we should choose ANSWER 3: a cute (1. general opinion) little (3. size) grey (7. colour) kitten.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: His team plays football ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or the place (where, when, how, how often, etc.) Many adverbs are formed from adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: He shook hands with a man ___ is a mayor.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'that' and 'who' for people in relative clauses.  'Whose' and 'whom' are used as objects.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Sarah always puts the blame ___ someone else.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them. In the test sentence ‘Sarah always puts the blame ____ someone else.’ we need to choose the preposition that is used after the noun ‘blame’ that means ‘the situation in which people say or think that someone or something did something wrong or is responsible for something bad happening’. We can use three prepositions after the noun ‘blame’: (1) ‘for’ (I always get the blame for his mistakes!); (2) ‘on’ (He stole the money but he’s trying to put the blame on me.); (3) ‘onto’ (It’s no use trying to shift the blame onto other people.). Among the test answers we can choose ANSWER 4: ‘on’.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: John is ill. He must stay ___ bed.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It's correct to stay 'in bed'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I'm not keen ___ yoga.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'keen on'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: How many natural ___ (a phenomenon) do you know?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are many nouns which have Greek or Latin origin. As a rule, they keep own endings: A PHENOMENON - TWO PHENOMENA.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It's too dark, I can't see ___ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the pronoun 'something' to refer to things in affirmative sentences, while 'anything' in negative ones. 'Any' and 'some' are pronouns which don't relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If Mike ___ (to return) early we ___ (to have) dinner with him.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about probable situations in the present or future we use Conditional 1: If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future/modal + present without 'to') or If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future + HAVE TO, OUGHT TO, BE TO + present without 'to').

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: "Carla: ""I've forgotten my e-mail password""."
options: Carla said that she has forgotten her e-mail password.
Carla said that she forgot her e-mail password.
Carla said that she had forgotten her e-mail password.
Carla said that she had been forgetting her e-mail password.

options_map.A: Carla said that she has forgotten her e-mail password.
options_map.B: Carla said that she forgot her e-mail password.
options_map.C: Carla said that she had forgotten her e-mail password.
options_map.D: Carla said that she had been forgetting her e-mail password.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Carla said that she had forgotten her e-mail password.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We change the Present Perfect to the Past Perfect in Reported Speech.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Single out the answer with the right word order:
options: The Olympics take place every four years.
Every four years take place the Olympics.
The Olympics take every four years place.
Take place the Olympics every four years.

options_map.A: The Olympics take place every four years.
options_map.B: Every four years take place the Olympics.
options_map.C: The Olympics take every four years place.
options_map.D: Take place the Olympics every four years.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: The Olympics take place every four years.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There is a certain word order in statements: Subject - Predicate - Object. The phrase 'take place' shouldn't be divided.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Bill and Richard _________ (to be) friends for many ages.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The action in this sentence started in the Past and continues in the Present. It means that Bill and Richard are still friends. In this case we should use the Present Perfect Tense:  has/have + Verb (-ed/Irregular)

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: David Beckham _____________ (to play) for Manchester United from 1993 to 2003.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Past simple is used to talk about finished actions and time. And in the test sentence ‘David Beckham ________ (to play) for Manchester United from 1993 to 2003.’ We are given the time-marker ‘from … to’ that we use to say when a past situation started and finished. Therefore, we are to choose ANSWER 1 (played).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I'm so tired of this town. I ___ (to move) to Paris.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: If we have a plan, ambition or intention to do something for the future we use 'be going to’. If we choose ANSWER 1 (am going to move), we create the context about the speaker’s future intentions that have been decided but have not been fully planned (referring to the past decision) that is expressed by the construction ‘be going to’.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Berlin _______________ (to found) in the 12th century.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we don't know who carries out the action, or it is obvious or unimportant to us, we use the Passive voice. The Passive is formed: BE + Past Participle. In this sentence the action took place at a certain time in the past, so we use the Past Simple Passive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ you make me a cup of coffee, please?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the modal verb 'could' when we ask somebody to do something.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Melanie has to ___ (to go in front of) because she is the leader in her squad.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verbs are verbs that consist of a verb and a particle and/or a preposition. Phrasal verbs are typical of spoken English or informal writing, e.g. letters to friends and articles in popular journalism. They cannot be understood based upon the meanings of the individual parts in isolation, thus, their meanings are unpredictable. The phrasal verb 'to go ahead' means 'to be in front of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to swim' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO SWIM - SWAM - SWUM

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jake said that he saw Jessica Alba ______ in the street.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use here 'herself' to show the importance of an object. In this sentence we mean that the fact of meeting a certain person - Jessica Alba - was very important for Jake. 'Himself' does not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I think this street is ___ in the town.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we compare a person or a thing with more than one person or one thing we use the superlative form of adjectives. If we use a one-syllable adjective '-est' to it.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The rain was falling ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or the place (where, when, how, how often, etc.) Many adverbs are formed from adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The singer, ______ I like a lot, is Corey Taylor.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: What' is a question word, it cannot be used here. We use 'which' for animals and objects. 'Whose' refers to possession and 'whom' is used as an object.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Caroline should understand that she takes responsibility ___ what is happening in her work and life.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'responsibility for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Mike was _____ the bus when I texted him.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'on the bus'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Your jacket is similar ___ mine.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'similar to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I can't remember all these __________ (a formula).
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are many nouns which have Greek or Latin origin. As a rule, they keep own endings: A FORMULA - TWO FORMULAE. 'Formulas' also can be used.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We haven't got _________ salt.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Much' is used before uncountable nouns. 'Many', 'a few' - before countable. We use 'some' in positive sentences.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If I __________ (to win) an Olympic medal I __________ (to dedicate) it to my family.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about imaginary situations which differ from real facts in the present we use Conditional 2: If-clause (if + Past Simple) - Main Clause (would/could + present without 'to'). The meaning of this sentence: in reality I'm not a sportsman, I only imagine.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: "Dexter: ""I'll read this book next month""."
options: Dexter said that he would read that book the month after.
Dexter said that he would read that book next month.
Dexter said that he  read that book the month after.
Dexter said that he had read that book next month.

options_map.A: Dexter said that he would read that book the month after.
options_map.B: Dexter said that he would read that book next month.
options_map.C: Dexter said that he  read that book the month after.
options_map.D: Dexter said that he had read that book next month.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Dexter said that he would read that book the month after.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We change the Future Simple to the Conditional in Reported Speech: will - would. Also we change time expressions: next month - the month after.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Single out the answer with the right word order?
options: My husband returns usually home at 7 p.m.
My husband usually returns home  at 7 p.m.
My husband returns home  at 7 p.m. usually.
My husband returns home at usually 7 p.m.

options_map.A: My husband returns usually home at 7 p.m.
options_map.B: My husband usually returns home  at 7 p.m.
options_map.C: My husband returns home  at 7 p.m. usually.
options_map.D: My husband returns home at usually 7 p.m.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: My husband usually returns home  at 7 p.m.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The adverb goes after the auxiliary verb. But if there is no auxiliary verb in the sentence, the adverb should be placed before the main verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: New York is  ___  city in the USA.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the article 'a' with singular countable nouns when we talk about them in general.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Don't disturb Tony! He ____________ (to write) a letter at the moment.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The phrase 'at the moment' means that the action is happening at this certain moment, right now. So, in this case we should always use the Present Continuous Tense. This Tense is formed: am/is/are + Verb-ing.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jill wiped the table after supper, took a shower and ___ (to go) to bed.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we talk about actions which happened one after another in the past we use the Past Simple Tense.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Susan ___ (to go) to the birthday party this weekend. Sarah invited her a week ago.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: If we have decided to do something or arranged to do something in the near future we use 'be going to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: These shoes ___ (to make) in Italy.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we don't know who carries out the action, or it is obvious or unimportant to us, we use the Passive voice. The Passive is formed: BE + Past Participle.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Don't run! The dog ______________ get furious.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the modal verb 'may' when it is possible that something will happen.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: They ___ (to raise a child) two children.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verbs are verbs that consist of a verb and a particle and/or a preposition. Phrasal verbs are typical of spoken English or informal writing, e.g. letters to friends and articles in popular journalism. They cannot be understood based upon the meanings of the individual parts in isolation, thus, their meanings are unpredictable. The phrasal verb 'to bring up' means 'to raise a child'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to take' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO TAKE - TOOK - TAKEN.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Is there ___ who can speak Italian?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Everybody' and 'nobody' do not relate to the meaning of the sentence. 'Anybody' is used in interrogative sentences, while 'somebody' is used in affirmative sentences.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Lily wants everything right now. She's too ___ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that the adjective 'patient' is used with the prefix 'im-'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Ted passed the test ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or the place (where, when, how, how often, etc.) Many adverbs are formed from adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: He is playing with the boy, ___ gave him a balloon two days ago.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'who' for people in relative clauses when 'who' is a subject. 'Whose' and 'whom' are used as objects. We use 'which' to refer to animals and objects.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: John announced the best solution ___ our problem.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'solution to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I usually go to the gym ____ Mondays and Thursdays.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'on Mondays'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Your essay is full ___ mistakes.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'full of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: There are a few _________ (an oasis) in deserts.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are many nouns which have Greek or Latin origin. As a rule, they keep own endings: AN OASIS - TWO OASES

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: There are ________ books on the shelf.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Many' is used before countable nouns. 'Much' and 'a little' - before uncountable. We use 'any' in negative sentences.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The police ___ (to arrest) her if they ___ (to catch) her.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about probable situations in the present or future we use Conditional 1: If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future/modal + present without 'to') or If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future + HAVE TO, OUGHT TO, BE TO + present without 'to').

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: "Teacher: "Don't be so lazy"."
options: Teacher asked us did not to be so lazy.
Teacher asked us not to be so lazy.
Teacher asked us did not be so lazy.
Teacher asked us to be not so lazy.

options_map.B: Teacher asked us not to be so lazy.
options_map.C: Teacher asked us did not be so lazy.
options_map.D: Teacher asked us to be not so lazy.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Teacher asked us not to be so lazy.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we need to transform a request into Reported Speech we use an introductory verb + the to-infinitive: asked not + to be.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Single out the answer with the right word order
options: You can show me the way to  Westminster Abbey?
Can show you me the way to  Westminster Abbey?

options_map.B: Can show you me the way to  Westminster Abbey?

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to ask a question with a modal verb we must place it in the first place: Modal Verb - Subject - Predicate - Object. 'Can' is a modal verb, 'you' - a subject, 'show' - a predicate, 'me the way to the Westminster Abbey' - an object.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My husband gave me ___ twenty five roses.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we use numerals before nouns we don't use any article.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Rachel ___ (to be) in Frankfurt since Sunday.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The action in this sentence started in the Past (on Monday) and continues in the Present. It means that Rachel is still in Frankfurt. In this case we should use the Present Perfect Tense: has/have + Verb (-ed/Irregular).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Abraham Lincoln ______________ (to become) the 16th President of the United States in 1860.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Past Simple Tense when we talk about actions which happened at a definite time in the past.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It's very cold today. I expect it ___ (to snow) tomorrow.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Simple Tense when we make predictions about the future with the verbs 'expect, think, believe, etc.'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The room ___ (to clean) tomorrow.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we don't know who carries out the action, or it is obvious or unimportant to us, we use the Passive voice. In this sentence we speak about the action which will be completed in the future: Will Be + Past Participle.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Carol is very ill. She ___ take medicines every day.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the modal verb 'must' when we talk about duties or when it is necessary to do something.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It's a great pity that Helen and Bob ___ (to separate)
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verbs are verbs that consist of a verb and a particle and/or a preposition. Phrasal verbs are typical of spoken English or informal writing, e.g. letters to friends and articles in popular journalism. They cannot be understood based upon the meanings of the individual parts in isolation, thus, their meanings are unpredictable. The phrasal verb 'to break up' means 'to separate'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to wake' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO WAKE - WOKE - WOKEN.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Lisa, do you want to give anybody these flowers? - No, I've bought them for ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When the same person is both the subject and the object in the sentence we place a reflexive pronoun after a verb or a preposition. 'Myself' is the right reflexive form of the personal pronoun 'I'. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jessy is being very ___ today!
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that the adjective 'polite' is used with the prefix 'im-'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The dog was waiting for him ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or the place (where, when, how, how often, etc.) Many adverbs are formed from adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Rachel told us the news, ______ we had already heard.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'which' or 'that' for things in relative clauses. 'Whose' and 'whom' are used as objects.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Nelly has experience ___ accounting.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'experience in'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I don't like to get up early ____ the morning.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'in the morning'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I'm always short ______ time.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'short of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: There are many ________ (a salmon) in these waters.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are some nouns which have the same form in the singular and in the plural: ONE SALMON - TWO SALMON.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I have ___ money left after shopping.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 'A little' is used before uncountable nouns. 'Many', 'a few' and 'few' - before countable.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If I _________ (to be) taller I _________ (to be) a model.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about imaginary situations which differ from real facts in the present we use Conditional 2: If-clause (if + Past Simple) - Main Clause (would/could + present without 'to'). The meaning of this sentence: in reality I'm not a model.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: "Jane: ""Mike plays the violin""."
options: Jane said that Mike played the violin.
Jane said that Mike had played the violin.
Jane said that Mike was playing the violin.
Jane said that Mike would play the violin.

options_map.A: Jane said that Mike played the violin.
options_map.B: Jane said that Mike had played the violin.
options_map.C: Jane said that Mike was playing the violin.
options_map.D: Jane said that Mike would play the violin.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Jane said that Mike played the violin.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We change the Present Simple to the Past Simple in Reported Speech.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Single out the sentence with the right word order:
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The right word order in the wh-question is: Question Word - Auxiliary - Subject. 'What' is a question word, 'is' - an auxiliary verb, ' your favourite colour' - a subject.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Everest is ___ highest mountain in the world.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'the' with all kinds of nouns when we talk about definite and specific things. 'The' also before nouns mentioned for the second time. Here: we know that there is the only highest mountain in the world.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Rob ___ (not / to finish) the task yet.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The action in this sentence started at an unstated time in the Past and continues in the Present. It means that Rob is still doing the task. In this case we should use the Present Perfect Tense: has / have + Verb (-ed/irregular).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I was sitting in the cafe when my phone ___ (to ring).
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: In this case the first action was in progress when suddenly something interrupted it. For a longer action we use the Past Continuous Tense. The second action was shorter so we should use the Past Simple Tense. The verb 'to ring' is irregular: RING - RANG - RUNG.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jerry is in Cardiff now. You ___________ (to see) him till Tuesday.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Simple Tense when we talk about common actions and facts which will happen in the future.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The ballots ___ (to count) several hours ago.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we don't know who carries out the action, or it is obvious or unimportant to us, we use the Passive voice. The Passive is formed: BE + Past Participle. In this sentence the action took place at a certain time in the past, so we use the Past Simple Passive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: You are sometimes totally unbearable! You ___ be more tolerant.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the modal verb 'should' when we give advice or recommend something.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: You play chess very well, I think you should ___ (to take part in) the school competition.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: In this sentence we are given the definition of one of four phrasal verbs ‘to take part in’. The phrasal verb ‘go in for’ has some meanings: (1) ‘to do something regularly, or to enjoy something’ (I don’t go in for surfing much.); (2) (BrE) ‘to take part in a competition, or to take an examination’ (She went in for the exam.); (3) (BrE) ‘to choose something as a subject of study or as your career’ (I am sure that she’s planning to go in for politics.). The second meaning of this phrasal verb suits the test sentence, thus, we are to choose ANSWER 4 (go in for) in the test.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to write' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO WRITE - WROTE - WRITTEN.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Vicky, if someone sends a message answer _____ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we need to refer to a person after 'someone', 'anyone' and 'no one' we use the personal pronoun 'they'. Here the pronoun has the position of the object. That is why we use the objective form - 'them'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This group of young people committed many ___ actions.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: In the test variants we are given the adjective ‘social’ with four prefixes dis-, un-, non-, anti-. The adjective ‘unsocial’ means ‘happening during days of the week or hours when most people do not have to work’ (Nobody wants to work unsocial hours.). The prefix ‘anti’ means ‘against, in opposition to, or opposite of’. The adjective ‘antisocial’ means (1) ‘harmful to society’ and (2) ‘often avoiding spending time with other people’. Its synonyms are ‘unfriendly’ and ‘cold’. There is even one more adjective ‘insocial’ that means ‘not sociable’.The words ‘dissociable’ and ‘non-sociable’ are nonce-words. Therefore, among the test variants we are to choose ANSWER 4 (antisocial).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Peter always dresses _________.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to add more information about a verb, an adjective, another adverb, a clause or a whole sentence. In the test sentence ‘Peter always dresses _________.’ we add more information about the verb ‘dress’.Adverbs have many different meanings and functions. They are especially important for indicating the time (when), manner (the way something happens or is done, how something happens), place (where), degree (how) and frequency (how often) of something. In the test we are given four variants: ‘smarty’, ‘smart’, ‘smartly’ and ‘smartful’ that have the same root morpheme ‘smart’ that has several meanings: (1) ‘stylish’; (2) ‘intelligent’; (3) ‘quick’; (4) ‘without respect’. As the test sentence is connected with clothes, we understand that we need to choose the first meaning of the adjective ‘smart’ for the test sentence: ‘Peter always dresses how? – in a stylish way’, therefore, we are to change the adjective ‘smart’ into the adverb of manner that is usually placed either after the main verb or after the object. Adverbs of manner are often formed from adjectives by adding -ly: bad – badly, brave bravely, sudden – suddenly. Thus, we need to add –ly to the adjective ‘smart’: ‘smart’ → ‘smartly’.The variants ‘smartful’ and ‘smarty’ are nonce-words.

We use them to refer to possession and ‘belonging’. We use possessive determiners before nouns: Is that your dress? But we use possessive pronouns without a noun: This handbag is very similar to mine.In the test sentence ‘It seems Mark and Jane have taken my umbrella because I can see only _______ on the shelf.’ there is not any noun after the omitted word: ‘I can see only what?’. Therefore, some possessive pronoun is omitted. As the context is given in the test: ‘…Mark and Jane have taken my umbrella …’, it is supposed that Mark and Jane (they) left their umbrella. Therefore, the possessive pronoun that correlates with the personal subject pronoun ‘they’ is ‘theirs’: ‘they’ (the personal subject pronoun) → ‘theirs’ (the possessive pronoun).Therefore, we choose ANSWER 4: theirs.

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The un- (= ‘not’) prefix is commonly attached to Latin derivatives that end in suffixes such as -ed and -able, resulting in adjectives such as unfounded, unassailable, and unbelievable.The adjective ‘reliable’ that means ‘able to be trusted to do or provide what is needed ’ (a reliable friend) has the suffix ‘able’. multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we compare a person or a thing with more than one person or one thing we use the superlative form of adjectives. If we use a one-syllable adjective we add '-est' to it.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: They live together ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or the place (where, when, how, how often, etc.) Many adverbs are formed from adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Paul finally met a lady, ___ helped him find the way to the cinema.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'who' for people in relative clauses when 'who' is a subject. 'Whose' and 'whom' are used as objects. We use 'which' to refer to animals and objects.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: He gave a poor excuse ___ his behavior.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'excuse for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I like to travel ___ summer.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'in summer'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: John is crazy ___ Mary.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There is an idiom ‘be crazy about sb/sth’ that means ‘to be very interested in something or love someone very much’: My sons are crazy about football. Therefore, among the test variants we are to choose ANSWER 3 (about).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I see ___ people outside.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Many' is used before countable nouns. 'Much' and 'a little' - before uncountable. We use 'any' in negative sentences.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I ___ (to try) to help you if you ___ (to tell) me what's wrong.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about probable situations in the present or future we use Conditional 1: If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future/modal + present without 'to') or If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future + HAVE TO, OUGHT TO, BE TO + present without 'to').

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: "Melanie: ""Where have you bought these shoes?"""
options: Melanie asked me where I bought those shoes.
Melanie asked me where did I buy those shoes.
Melanie asked me where had I had bought those shoes.
Melanie asked me where I had bought those shoes.

options_map.A: Melanie asked me where I bought those shoes.
options_map.B: Melanie asked me where did I buy those shoes.
options_map.C: Melanie asked me where had I had bought those shoes.
options_map.D: Melanie asked me where I had bought those shoes.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Melanie asked me where I had bought those shoes.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Melanie asked me where I had bought those shoes.' - this is the right word order in Reported Speech for special questions. We add 'where' before a pronoun and then place the auxiliary verb.  Here we change the Present Perfect into the Past Perfect.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Determine the answer with the right word order
options: Kyle will tell you this story in the park tomorrow.
Kyle will tell you tomorrow this story in the park.
Kyle  tomorrow will tell you this story in the park.
Kyle  will tell you this story tomorrow in the park.

options_map.A: Kyle will tell you this story in the park tomorrow.
options_map.B: Kyle will tell you tomorrow this story in the park.
options_map.C: Kyle  tomorrow will tell you this story in the park.
options_map.D: Kyle  will tell you this story tomorrow in the park.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Kyle will tell you this story in the park tomorrow.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There is a certain word order in statements: Subject - Verb - Object. In standard English we normally use the object of place before the object of time: in the park tomorrow.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Do you know when ___ Antarctica was officially discovered?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 'The' is not used before names of continents.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I ___ (to live) here since childhood and I think I know everyone in our village.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Since shows us that the action started in the past and continues up to now. That is why we use Present Perfect: has/have + Verb (-ed/Past Participle).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jake _______ (to roast) meat in the oven while Cara ________ (to knead) dough.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: While indicates simultaneous actions. In this case we use the Past Continuous Tense for both actions.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I ___ (to send) you photos when I get them.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: If a speaker suggests to do something voluntarily - we use the Future Simple.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active Voice sentence into the Passive one: Britain kept Napoleon on the island of Saint Helena.
options: Napoleon was been kept on the island of Saint Helena  by England.
Napoleon had kept on the island of Saint Helena  by England.
Napoleon kept on the island of Saint Helena  by England.
Napoleon was kept on the island of Saint Helena by England.

options_map.A: Napoleon was been kept on the island of Saint Helena  by England.
options_map.B: Napoleon had kept on the island of Saint Helena  by England.
options_map.C: Napoleon kept on the island of Saint Helena  by England.
options_map.D: Napoleon was kept on the island of Saint Helena by England.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Napoleon was kept on the island of Saint Helena by England.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The Passive Voice is formed according to this rule:  Subject - Be+ Past Participle - Preposition 'BY' - Agent (who or what carries out the action). The right form for the Past Simple Passive is: was/were + past participle or verb+ -ed

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ a doctor, I want to define the illnesses. Unfortunately I'm an IT specialist and don't have medicine knowledge.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Like means 'similar to'. It means that the speaker is not a doctor. 'As a doctor' means 'being a doctor'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Darling, could you ___ (to reverse, to move backward) the car? There's a large puddle near my door, I can't get out.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to back up' means 'to reverse, to move backward'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Little Johnny is a (an) ___ brilliant boy!
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Some words can make adjectives stronger. We call these words 'intensifiers'. Some of them are: very, really, pretty, absolutely. Remember that with strong adjectives (with extreme meaning) like 'brilliant' we use certain intensifiers. For example: exceptionally, completely, absolutely, totally, utterly, quite.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: She looked at him ________ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or a place (where, when, how, how often, etc.). They are formed by adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My grandmother enjoys ___ (to swim) in the sea.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Enjoy requires the Gerund. In this case the Gerund is used as the object of the verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: People joined a walk through the town __ memory __ the poet.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions before and after them: 'in memory of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The meeting is scheduled ___ Friday evening.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'on Friday evening'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Martin is looking for a job and a place to move in. He doesn't want to be overly dependent ___ his parents.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'dependent on'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Unfortunately, hunters kill many ___  every year.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are some nouns which have the same form in the singular and in the plural: ONE GROUSE - TWO GROUSE.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It was the worst birthday ever. ___ friends visited me.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Few is used with countable nouns and means 'Almost no friends visited me'. 'A few' is also used with countable nouns, but means 'Enough friends visited me'. It is a positive meaning and does not relate to the context. 'A little' and 'much' are used with uncountable nouns.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express disappointment with the present situation: I have to do this task. I don't want to do it.
options: If only I had done that task.
I wish I didn’t have to do that task.
I would do that task if I had to.
I didn't want to do that task but I had to.

options_map.A: If only I had done that task.
options_map.B: I wish I didn’t have to do that task.
options_map.C: I would do that task if I had to.
options_map.D: I didn't want to do that task but I had to.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: I wish I didn’t have to do that task.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To express disappointment with the present situation we usually use the construction [ I + wish + Past Simple]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a prefix to make a word negative: fair
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'fair - unfair'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Opt the answer with the right word order:
options: My grandfather a passionate numismatist was.
A passionate numismatist my grandfather was.
My grandfather was a passionate numismatist.

options_map.A: My grandfather a passionate numismatist was.
options_map.C: A passionate numismatist my grandfather was.
options_map.D: My grandfather was a passionate numismatist.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: My grandfather was a passionate numismatist.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There is a certain word order in statements: Subject - Verb - Object. 'My grandfather' is a subject, 'was' - an auxiliary verb, 'a passionate numismatist' - an object.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ Bronx is the third most densely populated county in the U.S.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The is not used before names of cities and suburbs, but there are some exceptions: the Hague, the Bronx, the Plains (Virginia).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Hey, Patrick! Don't forget, that the party ___ (to start) at 9 o'clock!
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use Present Simple to talk about scheduled events which will happen in the near future.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Kate was sleeping when her alarm clock ______( to go off).
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: In this case the first action was in progress when suddenly something interrupted it. For a longer action we use the Past Continuous Tense. The second action was shorter so we use the Past Simple Tense.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I _______ (to read) a newspaper when mom arrives tonight.
