multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Continuous Tense to show that some activity will be in progress at a certain point of time in the future

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active Voice sentence into the Passive one: It is known that pirates kidnapped Julius Caesar on the way across the Aegean Sea.
options: It is known that Julius Caesar had kidnapped by pirates on the way across the Aegean Sea.
It is known that Julius Caesar was kidnapped by pirates on the way across the Aegean Sea.
It is known that Julius Caesar was kidnapping by pirates on the way across the Aegean Sea.
It is known that Julius Caesar kidnapped pirates on the way across the Aegean Sea.

options_map.A: It is known that Julius Caesar had kidnapped by pirates on the way across the Aegean Sea.
options_map.B: It is known that Julius Caesar was kidnapped by pirates on the way across the Aegean Sea.
options_map.C: It is known that Julius Caesar was kidnapping by pirates on the way across the Aegean Sea.
options_map.D: It is known that Julius Caesar kidnapped pirates on the way across the Aegean Sea.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: It is known that Julius Caesar was kidnapped by pirates on the way across the Aegean Sea.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The Passive Voice is formed according to this rule:  Subject - Be+ Past Participle - Preposition 'BY' - Agent (who or what carries out the action). The right form for Past Simple Passive is: was/were + past participle or verb+ -ed. Other answers are incorrect or illogical.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Paula wants to lose 10 kilos. But she  _____ no attempt to reach this aim.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to make an attempt'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The bus ___ (to stop working, functioning) so I had to go on foot.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to break down' means 'to stop working, functioning'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to overthrow' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO OVERTHROW - OVERTHREW - OVERTHROWN.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___  the accident the flight was delayed.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The accident' is the reason why the flight was delayed. To introduce a reason we could use 'owing to' and 'since'. But you should remember that after 'since' we place a clause. Linking words of reason that are followed by a noun are: owing to, due to, because of.  Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Mark is a pretty ___ child.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Six-year-old is the only correct answer. Remember that such adjectives are constructed in this word order: number-year-old.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The politician _____ overcame uneasy and awkward questions from journalists.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or a place (where, when, how, how often, etc.). They are formed by adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My little brother wants ___ (to play) football again.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Want requires the Infinitive. We cannot use the Gerund with this verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My little sister likes fairy tales ____ Hans Christian Andersen.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'fairy tales (poems and etc) by...'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It's always uneasy to find an interesting book ____ hundreds of others  in the bookstore.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'to find among others' when we mean 'to discover the necessary thing in the midst of others'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jane is not very keen ___ sport.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'keen on'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Tom Harris, a 36-year-old firefighter, saved 3 _____ after a fire broke out in a house.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Some nouns have spelling changes in plural. A LIFE - NINE LIVES.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I need ___ money. Jeremy, could you lend me 3 dollars?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: A few is used with countable nouns and means 'some'. 'A little' is used with uncountable nouns and also means 'some'. 'Any' is used in negative sentences. 'Many' is used with countable nouns.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express regret about the past: It's a pity that I didn't know her before.
options: I would have known her before.
I would like to know her before.
I wish I have known her before.
I wish I had known her before.

options_map.A: I would have known her before.
options_map.B: I would like to know her before.
options_map.C: I wish I have known her before.
options_map.D: I wish I had known her before.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: I wish I had known her before.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to show regret about the past we usually use the construction [I + wish + Past Perfect]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a prefix to make a word negative: competent
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'competent - incompetent'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Opt the answer with the right word order?
options: Robert gave to the child a cookie.
Robert gave a cookie to the child.
A cookie Robert gave to the child.
A cookie gave Robert the child.

options_map.A: Robert gave to the child a cookie.
options_map.B: Robert gave a cookie to the child.
options_map.C: A cookie Robert gave to the child.
options_map.D: A cookie gave Robert the child.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Robert gave a cookie to the child.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we say 'give something to somebody' we place the indirect object after the direct object: Robert gave a cookie to the child. But when we omit 'to' the indirect object should be placed in front of the direct object. Answers 3 and 4 do not follow the word order: Subject - Verb - Object.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The last eruption of ___ Kilimanjaro volcano happened about 200 years ago.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When the word 'volcano' is used, the definite article 'THE' should be placed before the name of the volcano.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Where's Monica? I haven't seen her since Monday. - She's at home. She ___ (recently / to break) her arm.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: If we see in the present the result  of the event which happened in the past - we use the Present Perfect. Here: Monica's broken arm is the result of some accident of the past. The Present Perfect Tense is formed:  has/have + Verb (-ed/Past Participle).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The children were making origami when their babysitter ___ (to call) them to dinner.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: In this case the first action was in progress when suddenly the second one interrupted it. For a longer action we use the Past Continuous Tense. The second action was shorter so we use the Past Simple Tense.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If I'm elected the Head of the company, I _____ (to raise) wages.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we talk about promises we usually use the Future Simple Tense.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active Voice sentence into the Passive one: The Congress signed the Declaration  on July 4 in 1776.
options: The Declaration had signed by the Congress on July 4 in 1776.
The Congress was signed by the Declaration on July 4 in 1776.
The Declaration has been signed by the Congress on July 4 in 1776.
The Declaration was signed by the Congress on July 4 in 1776.

options_map.A: The Declaration had signed by the Congress on July 4 in 1776.
options_map.B: The Congress was signed by the Declaration on July 4 in 1776.
options_map.C: The Declaration has been signed by the Congress on July 4 in 1776.
options_map.D: The Declaration was signed by the Congress on July 4 in 1776.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: The Declaration was signed by the Congress on July 4 in 1776.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: In this sentence the action took place at a certain time in the past, so we use the Past Simple Passive: was/were + Past Participle. Answer 2 is illogical because the Declaration cannot be the doer of an action.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It is important to me to _____ business with honest partners.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to do business'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Melanie _______ (to devote the day) to her kids and parents.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to give over' means 'to dedicate all the time to somebody or to something'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to backslide' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO BACKSLIDE - BACKSLID - BACKSLID.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jeremy works hard ___ to prove he deserves to get a higher position.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To prove he deserves to get a higher position is a purpose why Jeremy works hard. When we introduce a purpose we use 'in order/so as + to-infinitive' or 'so (that)/in order (that) + clause'. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I bought ______ (riding/beautiful/black) boots yesterday.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There is a certain word order in sentences with two or more adjectives: OPINION-SIZE-AGE-SHAPE-COLOUR-ORIGIN-MATERIAL-PURPOSE. Here: beautiful (opinion) black (colour) riding (purpose)

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Our friends ________ invited us to visit their new home in Stradford.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or a place (where, when, how, how often, etc.) They are formed by adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Stacey stopped ___ (to drink) some water. She made a pause during her jogging.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Some verbs can be used both with the Gerund and the Infinitive. But in some cases the meaning of the sentence becomes different. Compare: stopped to drink - stopped one activity in order to start another one / stopped drinking - she is not drinking anymore.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The government will certainly give an appropriate reply ___ the challenge thrown by radical parties.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'a reply to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: What's the distinction ______ hardware and software?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'distinction between'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Our transport system is very similar ___ Berlin's one.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'similar to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: A stranger gave a beggar two _______ (a loaf) of bread and a bottle of water.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Some nouns have spelling changes: A LOAF - LOAVES.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Dear, have you bought ___ apples?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We usually use 'any' in questions.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express the idea when you want someone to do something in the present or future: It's late. Don't go there alone.
options: If only you hadn't gone there alone.
I wish you hadn't gone there alone.
I'd rather you went there alone.
I'd rather you didn't go there alone.

options_map.A: If only you hadn't gone there alone.
options_map.B: I wish you hadn't gone there alone.
options_map.C: I'd rather you went there alone.
options_map.D: I'd rather you didn't go there alone.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: I'd rather you didn't go there alone.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we need to express the idea when you want someone to do something in the present or future we usually use the construction [would rather + subject + Past Simple]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a suffix to form an adjective from a given word: guilt
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'guilt - guilty'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Opt the answer with the right word order
options: Why can't we have a cup of coffee at first?
Why we can't have a cup of coffee at first?
Can't why we have a cup of coffee at first?
Why have  we can't  a cup of coffee at first?

options_map.A: Why can't we have a cup of coffee at first?
options_map.B: Why we can't have a cup of coffee at first?
options_map.C: Can't why we have a cup of coffee at first?
options_map.D: Why have  we can't  a cup of coffee at first?

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Why can't we have a cup of coffee at first?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The right word order in the wh-question is: Question Word - Auxiliary or Modal - Subject - Main Verb - Object. 'Why' is a question word, 'can' - a modal verb, 'we' - a subject, 'have' - main verb, 'a cup of coffee at first' - an object.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It has been announced that ___ Pope is going to visit Warsaw.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We know that there is the only Pope in the world, so we use definite article 'the'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Samuel ___ (not to leave) the office yet. He wants to finish his report by tomorrow morning.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The action in this sentence started at an unstated time in the Past and continues in the Present. It means that  Samuel is still in the office. In this case we should use the Present Perfect Tense:  has/have + Verb (-ed/Past Participle).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Benjamin ___ (to watch) a movie before Alison ___ (to come) in.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Past Perfect Continuous emphasizes the duration of an action in the past before another one. We cannot use Past Continuous because this Tense wouldn't show that the first action started before the second one.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Luke ___ (to let) us know when he finds the keys to the apartment.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Simple Tense when we talk about common actions and facts which will happen in the future.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active Voice sentence into the Passive one: French sculptor Frederic Auguste Bartholdi designed the statue of Liberty.
options: The statue of Liberty has been designed by French sculptor Frederic Auguste Bartholdi.
The statue of Liberty designed by French sculptor Frederic Auguste Bartholdi.
French sculptor Frederic Auguste Bartholdi was designed by the statue of Liberty.
The statue of Liberty was designed by French sculptor Frederic Auguste Bartholdi.

options_map.A: The statue of Liberty has been designed by French sculptor Frederic Auguste Bartholdi.
options_map.B: The statue of Liberty designed by French sculptor Frederic Auguste Bartholdi.
options_map.C: French sculptor Frederic Auguste Bartholdi was designed by the statue of Liberty.
options_map.D: The statue of Liberty was designed by French sculptor Frederic Auguste Bartholdi.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: The statue of Liberty was designed by French sculptor Frederic Auguste Bartholdi.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: In this sentence the action took place at in the past, so we use the Past Simple Passive: was/were + Past Participle. Answer 3 is illogical because the statue of Liberty cannot be the doer of an action.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My neighbors _______ a terrible noise every evening.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to make a noise'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Oh, don't pay attention to me, ___  (to continue) your conversation, please.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to carry on' means 'to go on or continue with something'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose two forms of the verb 'to tear' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO TEAR - TORE - TORN.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: John had been playing football all morning. ___ he's exhausted.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we talk about a result we use 'so, therefore, as a result, for this reason'. Notice that they are usually come at the beginning of the sentence but it is possible for 'so' and 'therefore' to take also a middle position. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Audi or BMW: which do you like ___ ?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It's correct to say 'which do you like better?'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Our team played ______ last month.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or a place (where, when, how, how often, etc.). They are formed by adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jeremy stopped ___ (to smoke) a year ago. He doesn't want to start smoking anymore.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Some verbs can be used both with the Gerund and the Infinitive. But in some cases the meaning of the sentence becomes different. Compare: stopped to smoke - stopped one activity in order to start another one / stopped smoking - he doesn't smoke anymore.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: His fear __ flying is always a problem.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'fear of'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: She always stands out for what she believes __ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'believe in'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Her husband was accused ___ cheating with a 26-year-old model.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'accused of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It's too dark in the room, I can hardly see ___ here.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'any / anything' in negative sentences and in positive sentences with 'never, hardly, without'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If Charlie ___ (to leave) the house earlier, he ___ (to be) late for work.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about past unreal condition we use: If-clause (if + Past Perfect) - Main Clause (would have + past participle).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a suffix to form a noun from a given word: recover
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'recovery'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Pick out the answer with the right word order:
options: Trouble may I you for a napkin?
I may you trouble for a napkin?
May trouble I you for a napkin?
May I trouble you for a napkin?

options_map.A: Trouble may I you for a napkin?
options_map.B: I may you trouble for a napkin?
options_map.C: May trouble I you for a napkin?
options_map.D: May I trouble you for a napkin?

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: May I trouble you for a napkin?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to ask a question with a modal verb we must place it in the first place: Modal Verb - Subject - Verb - Object. 'May' is a modal verb, 'I' - a subject, 'trouble' - verb, 'you for the napkin' - an object.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: They have been married for __ sixteen years.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we use numerals before nouns we don't use articles.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It's just tactlessly of her. I _______ (to wait) for her all day and she's still not here.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we talk about unspecified period of time and an action which started before now and continues in the present - we use the Present Perfect Continuous. Also this tense shows that the speaker wants to highlight a process rather than a result.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My brother _______ (to look for) a job for 2 months before they _______ (to employ) him.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The action in the first part (had been looking for) took place before the action in the second one (employed). Another important moment is that the speaker focuses on the process rather than the action (for 2 months). That is why we use the Past Perfect Continuous in the first part.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: By the time you write the report I ___ (to leave).
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Perfect to show that one action will be completed before another one in the future. Here: I will leave before you finish the report.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active Voice sentence into the Passive one: The discovery of Pluto took place in 1930.
options: The discovery of Pluto was taken place in 1930.

options_map.D: The discovery of Pluto was taken place in 1930.

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The Passive Voice is formed according to this rule:  Subject - Be+ Past Participle - Preposition 'BY' - Agent (who or what carries out the action). The right form for the Past Simple Passive is: was/were + past participle or verb+ -ed.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Garry is going to _______ an exam next week.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to take an exam'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We had a quarrel last night but we could ___ (to forgive each other) in the morning.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to make up' means 'to forgive each other'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to seek' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO SEEK - SOUGHT - SOUGHT.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ rescue teams had been searching the lost climbers all night, they couldn't find any trace of them.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to show that there is a surprising contrast between two statements in one sentence we use 'although, though, even though' and 'despite/in spite of + -ing/noun/pronoun'. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Our breakfast turned out to be ________. So we wrote a complaint letter to the kitchen manager.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Inedible describes food that is not suitable for eating.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: - What time are we meeting? - At seven o'clock _____.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or a place (where, when, how, how often, etc.). They are formed by adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Tracey forgot ___ (to call) her grandfather. He had been waiting for that call so much but she didn't make it.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Some verbs can be used both with the Gerund and the Infinitive. But in some cases the meaning of the sentence becomes different. Compare: forgot to call - forgot that she needed to call / forgot calling - she called him but she forgot that fact.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Do you have an allergic reaction ___ antibiotics?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'reaction to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: They haven't replied ___ my plea yet.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'to reply to something'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The Tower of Pisa is crowded ___ tourists all the year round.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'crowded with'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: You can see several _____ in the Zoo.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are some nouns which have the same form in the singular and in the plural: A MOOSE - THREE MOOSE.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We cannot afford a dinner in this restaurant. We have ___ dollars left.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: A little and 'much' are used before uncountable nouns. 'Many' and 'a few'  - before countable ones. 'Many' doesn't relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Form a compound adjective from two words: slow + move
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'slow-moving'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Pick out the answer with the right word order?
options: My brother finds  always a way out of any situation.
Always my brother finds a way out of any situation.
My brother finds a way out of any situation always.
My brother always finds a way out of any situation.

options_map.A: My brother finds  always a way out of any situation.
options_map.B: Always my brother finds a way out of any situation.
options_map.C: My brother finds a way out of any situation always.
options_map.D: My brother always finds a way out of any situation.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: My brother always finds a way out of any situation.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The adverb goes after the auxiliary verb. But if there is no auxiliary verb in the sentence, the adverb should be placed before the main verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I heard ___ dog barking somewhere in the slum.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the article 'a' with singular countable nouns when we talk about them in general.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The next bus ___ at 9 o'clock this morning.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To talk about schedule we use Present Simple.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Oh, how I wish it ___ (not to be) so windy.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: If we talk about wishes and refer to the future or present we use the Past Simple.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I ___ (to call) you when I ___ (to come) home.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To talk about the future we often use clauses with 'when, after, until'. We use the present tense inside them and future tense in the main sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active Voice sentence into the Passive one: He's fixing a laptop at the moment.
options: The laptop is being fixing at the moment.
The laptop is been fixed at the moment.
The laptop is being fixed at the moment.
The laptop has been fixed at the moment.

options_map.A: The laptop is being fixing at the moment.
options_map.B: The laptop is been fixed at the moment.
options_map.C: The laptop is being fixed at the moment.
options_map.D: The laptop has been fixed at the moment.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: The laptop is being fixed at the moment.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 'Is being fixed' is the right form of the Present Progressive Passive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jillian was very disappointed that she has ___ a mistake.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to make a mistake'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I'm ill and feel very weak. I have to ___ (to cancel) the meeting.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to call something off' means 'to cancel something'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to rive' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO RIVE - RIVED - RIVEN / RIVED

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___  investigators didn't find any evidence of Mr. Clark's involvement in hijacking, he was imprisoned.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to show a conflict between the main clause and the statement in the subordinate clause we can use 'although (and its synonyms), while, whilst or whereas'. Note that 'while' and 'whilst' are used mostly in formal contexts. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It is necessary to reduce ___ expenses in the nearest future.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that the adjective 'essential' is used with the prefix 'non-'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Derek, please, visit me as fast as you can! I need your help ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or a place (where, when, how, how often, etc.)They are formed by adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Clark agreed ___ (to tell) me the truth.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Agree requires the Infinitive. We cannot use the Gerund with this verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I have a recipe ___  paella with seafood. I can give it to you.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'recipe for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Sarah should be very attentive with food. She is allergic ___ peanuts.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'allergic to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Some peculiarities of the language should be noted in _______.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are many nouns which have Greek or Latin origin. As a rule, they keep own endings: ONE PARENTHESIS - TWO PARENTHESES.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: How ___ questions are you going to ask in your interview?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Many is used before countable nouns. 'Much' and 'a little' - before uncountable ones. We use 'any' in negative and interrogative sentences.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express regret about the past: I regret that I watched that movie.
options: I wish I hadn't watched that movie.
I wish I didn't watch that movie.
I wouldn't have watched that movie.

options_map.A: I wish I hadn't watched that movie.
options_map.B: I wish I didn't watch that movie.
options_map.C: I wouldn't have watched that movie.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: I wish I hadn't watched that movie.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to show regret about the past we usually use the construction [I + wish + Past Perfect]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a suffix to form an adjective from a given word: efficiency
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'efficient'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Pick out the answer with the right word order
options: You easily can lose your friend's trust.
You can lose easily your friend's trust.
You can easily lose your friend's trust.
Easily you can lose your friend's trust.

options_map.A: You easily can lose your friend's trust.
options_map.B: You can lose easily your friend's trust.
options_map.C: You can easily lose your friend's trust.
options_map.D: Easily you can lose your friend's trust.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: You can easily lose your friend's trust.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The adverb 'easily' must be placed after the auxiliary verb 'can'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The travel company made us ______ advantageous offer.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use articles 'a/an' to show the quantity - only one. 'An' is used before words starting with sounds [a], [e], [i], [o], [u]

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Dave ___ (to visit) his Granny every month.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we talk about things in general, permanent situations and states or things which happen sometimes, we use the Present Simple Tense:  he/she/it +  Verb + -s(es).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The children ___ (to watch) 'The Hunger Games' when suddenly the light ___  (to go) out.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The first action was in progress when suddenly the second one interrupted it. For a longer action we use the Past Continuous Tense. The second action was shorter so we use the Past Simple Tense.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Spring has come at last. It ___ (to be) sunny in several days.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Simple Tense when we talk about actions which will certainly happen in the future and which we cannot control.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The novel 'The old man and the sea' ___ (to write) by Ernest Hemingway in 1951.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Sometimes we need to change a sentence from the Active Voice into the Passive Voice. We can also mention a person who carries out the action. In this case we use the Passive Voice and form a sentence according to this rule:  Subject - Be+ Past Participle - Preposition 'BY' - Agent (who or what carries out the action). Also, we should use the Past Simple Passive Voice In this sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Mila, could you _____ me a favor? Please, don't say those words about John anymore.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to do a favor'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Drake, I've ________ (to choose) four T-shirts. Which one suits me better?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to pick out' means 'to choose'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to lie' (to be in a horizontal position) according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO LIE - LAY - LAIN. The verb 'to lie' (not to tell truth) is regular: TO LIE - LIED - LIED.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___, we all were happy to get home finally.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to summarise what we have said or written before we use these linking words: 'in a nutshell, to conclude, in conclusion, in brief, in summary'. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Well, I've got an idea how to transform this terrible place into a ______ cosy shelter.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Lovely' means 'charming', while 'loving' means - 'feeling love', 'beloved' means - 'loved very much' and 'loveless' means - 'unloved'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It's cold outside. You have to dress up  _______ !
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or a place (where, when, how, how often, etc.). They are formed by adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Mrs. Burton seemed ___ (to be) happy.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Seem requires the Infinitive. We cannot use the Gerund with this verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Paul fell heir _____ his grandfather's fortune and property.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'to fall heir to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Harry will be late for the performance ___ an extremely long traffic jam.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'because of' to show the reason.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The dog was totally obedient ______ Mike.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'obedient to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: How many _______ (an axis) has the Earth?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The noun 'axis' has the irregular plural form: AXIS - AXES.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: That event was described in ________ Italian newspaper. I don't know its title exactly.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'some' in positive sentences and 'any' in negative ones before countable or uncountable nouns. 'Many' and 'a few' are used before plural countable nouns.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express the idea when you want someone to do something in the present or future: I don't want you to stay there for a long time.
options: I'd rather you hadn't stayed there for a long time.
I'd rather you didn't stay there for a long time.
I wish you stay there for a long time.
I wish you stayed there for a long time.

options_map.A: I'd rather you hadn't stayed there for a long time.
options_map.B: I'd rather you didn't stay there for a long time.
options_map.C: I wish you stay there for a long time.
options_map.D: I wish you stayed there for a long time.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: I'd rather you didn't stay there for a long time.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we need to express the idea when you want someone to do something in the present or future we usually use the construction [would rather + subject + Past Simple]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Find the correct word formation chain (noun - adjective - verb): analysis
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'analyst - analytical - analyse'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Pick the answer with the right word order:
options: Yesterday it was his car that stolen.
That stolen car was his yesterday.
It was his car that was stolen yesterday.
It was that his car stolen yesterday.

options_map.A: Yesterday it was his car that stolen.
options_map.B: That stolen car was his yesterday.
options_map.C: It was his car that was stolen yesterday.
options_map.D: It was that his car stolen yesterday.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: It was his car that was stolen yesterday.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Cleft sentences with 'it' are formed in this way: it + to be + object + that. We use this structure to focus on the information that we put in the first place. Here: it's important to say 'it was his car' - not someone else's one.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: His grandparents _______ (to be) married for 60 years.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The action in this sentence started in the Past and continues in the Present. It means that his grandparents got married 60 years ago and are still married. In this case we should use the Present Perfect Tense:  has/have + Verb (-ed/Past Participle).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Maria ___ (to study) at the Ontario Secondary School from 2008 to 2010
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Past Simple Tense when we talk about actions which happened at a definite time in the past. If we have a regular form of a verb in a sentence, we add '-ed'. Irregular forms should be memorized.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: By next October, I __________ (to finish) the research.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The Future Perfect helps to express the idea that one action will happen before another one or the certain time point in the future.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The Mona Lisa ___ (to paint) in 1503-1505.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we don't know who carries out the action, or it is obvious or unimportant to us, we use the Passive voice. The Passive is formed: BE + Past Participle. In this sentence the action took place at a certain time in the past, so we use the Past Simple Passive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Pete has ___ money by selling luxury cars.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to make money'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I'm not a person who can ___ (to tolerate) teenagers.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to put up with' means 'to tolerate'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to grind' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO GRIND - GROUND - GROUND.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: All the given plans opened for us a wide range of opportunities to release our potential. ___ they tell us about the competition and huge risks.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to add some extra information to the point we can use these linking words: furthermore, moreover, as well as, too, also, besides.  Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I've run 10 kilometres and feel _______ exhausted.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Some words can make adjectives stronger. We call these words 'intensifiers'. Some of them are: very, really, pretty, absolutely. Remember that with strong adjectives (with extreme meaning) like 'exhausted' we use certain intensifiers. For example: exceptionally, completely, absolutely, totally, utterly, quite.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Darren was running as _____ as he could.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'as fast as'. Remember that the word 'fast' do not change its form when we use it an adverb or adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The newspaper reported the party ___ (to win) the election.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Report requires the Gerund. In this case the Gerund is used as the object of the verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Locals are asking the city authorities to build a fence ______ the central park.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'a fence around something'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ my humble opinion, the plot of this book is overextended.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'in somebody's opinion'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Felix is mad ___ 'Queen' and 'Slipknot'.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'mad about' in the meaning of 'being a fan of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Scientists say that stars called supergiants have ____ (a radius) many times larger than that of our planet.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are many nouns which have Greek or Latin origin. As a rule, we memorize their forms: A RADIUS - TWO RADII. 'Radiuses' also can be used.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: How ___ paper do we use in the office daily?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Much is used before uncountable nouns. 'Many' and 'a few'  - before countable. 'Some' do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If Drake ___ (to have) time he ___ (to study) better.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about past unreal condition we use: If-clause (if + Past Perfect) - Main Clause (would have + past participle). In reality Drake didn't have time to study better.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Find the correct word formation chain (noun - adjective - verb): assassination
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'assassin - assassinated - assassinate'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Pick the answer with the right word order?
options: Ashley bought a new white mink fur coat a week ago.
Ashley bought a white new mink fur coat a week ago.
Ashley bought a new mink white fur coat a week ago.
Ashley bought a white mink new fur coat a week ago.

options_map.A: Ashley bought a new white mink fur coat a week ago.
options_map.B: Ashley bought a white new mink fur coat a week ago.
options_map.C: Ashley bought a new mink white fur coat a week ago.
options_map.D: Ashley bought a white mink new fur coat a week ago.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Ashley bought a new white mink fur coat a week ago.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There is a certain word order in statements with the Present Simple Tense: Subject - Auxiliary - Object. When we need to use many adjectives in one sentence, they should be placed in the following order: Opinion - Size - Age - Shape - Colour - Origin - Material - Purpose. 'New' defines age, 'white' refers to colour and 'mink' - to material.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: There is ____ table and four chairs in the kitchen.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the article 'a' with singular countable nouns  to show quantity - only one.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The weather ___ (to improve). I think we can go roller skating to the park soon.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Present Continuous in case of changing situations.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: In the cafe we ___ (to try) some delicious food, ___ (to drink) some wine and then we ___ (to walk) a lot in the city centre.
options: were trying / were drinking / were walking

options_map.A: were trying / were drinking / were walking

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we talk about actions which happened one after the other in the past we use the Past Simple Tense.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Darrel has realised too late that he ________ (to wait) for Jill for more than 3 hours when her aircraft lands.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The Future Perfect Continuous (like the Future Perfect) expresses the idea that an action will continue up until another one or certain time point in the Future. But the Future Perfect Continuous is more concentrated on the duration. We use it when it is important for us to emphasise 'how long' something will be in progress in the future: for an hour, for a week, for a year, etc.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active Voice sentence into the Passive one: The company is still constructing the building.
options: The building is still been constructed.
The building is still being constructed.
The building is still have being constructed.

options_map.B: The building is still been constructed.
options_map.C: The building is still being constructed.
options_map.D: The building is still have being constructed.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: The building is still being constructed.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Present Continuous in this sentence. Therefore we should use the appropriate form of the Passive - [auxiliary] + [being] + [verb+-ed / Past Participle].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Please, ___ your seats and fasten belts.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to take/have a seat'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I hate job interviews because it always seems like they ______ (to look arrogantly) me.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to look down on' means 'to look arrogantly and contemptuously'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Sure, you may take my phablet ________ you don't damage it.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to express a condition we usually use these linking words: as long as, provided/providing (that).  Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The performance was not brilliant, but I found it _______ interesting.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Some words can make adjectives weaker. We call these words mitigators. Some of them are: rather, a bit, a little bit, slightly, fairly. Intensifiers like 'completely, exceptionally' are used with extreme adjectives. Remember that 'enough' goes after the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I don't know what is going on! Jake _____ ignored me when I tried to talk to him.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Very often we use adverbs as intensifiers. It means that they help us emphasise something. Remember that adverbs are formed by adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Mr. Johnattan didn't mind _______ (to help) me.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Not to mind requires the Gerund. In this case the Gerund is used as the object of the verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: There are a lot of advantages ___ working as a stewardess.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'advantage in'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ all our previous troubles we've got another crashing news today.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'in addition to'. Other options do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Max moved into a new  place. He has to get accustomed ____ it.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'accustomed to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The meeting of ___ (alumna) will be held on Saturday.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are many nouns which have Greek or Latin origin. As a rule, they keep own endings: A ALUMNA - TWO ALUMNAE.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We live a boring life. We never go ______ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'some' in positive clauses while 'any' - in negative. 'Never' refers to negative meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If Julia ___ (to be) lucky, she ___ (to be taken) on this prestigious job.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about probable situations in the present or future we use Conditional 1: If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future/modal + present without 'to').

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Find the correct word formation chain (noun - adjective - verb): agitation
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'agitator - agitated - agitate'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Select the answer with the right word order?
options: Who had been sleeping during the flight the man  woke up.
The man during the flight who had been sleeping woke up.
The man woke up who had been sleeping during the flight.
The man who had been sleeping during the flight woke up.

options_map.A: Who had been sleeping during the flight the man  woke up.
options_map.B: The man during the flight who had been sleeping woke up.
options_map.C: The man woke up who had been sleeping during the flight.
options_map.D: The man who had been sleeping during the flight woke up.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: The man who had been sleeping during the flight woke up.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The subject is normally placed before the predicate. Note, that very often the subject is not a single word. Here: 'The man who had been sleeping during the flight' - is the subject. Then, you should pay attention to the word order inside this phrase: the man - is on the first place and relative clause with 'who' follows it.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The most famous carnival is celebrated in ___ Brazil.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The' is not used before names of countries, but there are some exceptions: the Netherlands, the Argentine, the Vatican City, the Sudan.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Origami ___ (to be) his hobby since childhood.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The action in this sentence started in the Past (childhood) and continues in the Present. It means that he is still fond of origami. In this case we should use the Present Perfect Tense:  has/have + Verb (-ed/Past Participle)

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Uma ___ (to visit) Moscow when she ___ (to be) young.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Past Simple Tense when we talk about actions which happened at a certain time in the past. Here: when she was young.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: - It's so stuffy here!  - I ______ (to open) the window.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Simple Tense when someone suggests to do something voluntarily.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Unfortunately all rooms in this hostel  ___ (already / to book). We need to look for another hostel.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The correct form of the Present Perfect Passive is: [have/has] + been + [verb+ -ed / Past Participle].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Their project ______ (is successful) very fine.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to work out' means 'to be successful'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to quit' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO QUIT - QUIT - QUIT.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ it was sunny, we took sunglasses and a parasol to shade skin from the light.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It was sunny' is the reason why we took sunglasses and a parasol. To give a reason for a certain situation we use 'seeing that, seeing as, as, because, since' + clause. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It was _______ of Laura to keep silent in response to a stranger's abuse in the subway.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Sensitive', 'sentimental' and 'sensual' don't relate to the meaning of the sentence. In this sentence we speak about reasonable - 'sensible' decision.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: _______ speaking, this song is utter garbage.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to use the adverb 'bluntly'. It means 'direct manner of speaking'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This car needs ___ (to clean).
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Some verbs can be used both with the Gerund and the Infinitive. But in some cases the meaning of the sentence becomes different. Compare:  needs to clean - somebody has the necessity in cleaning / the car needs cleaning - the car needs to be cleaned by somebody.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Her memory ___ traveling in Europe will stay with her for a long time.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'memory of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It's not polite to leave ___ saying goodbye.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'without saying'. Other answers are illogical.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Surely he's capable ___ winning the prize.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'capable of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: They watched the performance through ______ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation:
Some nouns are always plural: 
SCISSORS / GLASSES /
TROUSERS / JEANS /
SHORTS / TIGHTS /
PYGAMAS / NEWS / BINOCULARS etc.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: They have finally managed to complete the project without ___ help.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'some' in positive sentences and 'any' in negative ones. 'Without' refers to the negative meaning. 'Many' and 'a few' do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express disappointment with the present situation: George has to go shopping with his wife. But he doesn't want to.
options: George wishes he would go shopping with his wife.
George wished he hadn't gone shopping with his wife.
George wishes he didn't have to go shopping with his wife.
George wouldn't go shopping with his wife if he wanted.

options_map.A: George wishes he would go shopping with his wife.
options_map.B: George wished he hadn't gone shopping with his wife.
options_map.C: George wishes he didn't have to go shopping with his wife.
options_map.D: George wouldn't go shopping with his wife if he wanted.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: George wishes he didn't have to go shopping with his wife.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To express disappointment with the present situation we usually use the construction [ I + wish + Past Simple]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Select the answer with the right word order:
options: Hardly had Tom the house reached, it started to snow heavily.
Hardly Tom had reached the house, it started to snow heavily.
Hardly had Tom reached the house, it started to snow heavily.
Hardly had reached the house Tom, it started to snow heavily.

options_map.A: Hardly had Tom the house reached, it started to snow heavily.
options_map.B: Hardly Tom had reached the house, it started to snow heavily.
options_map.C: Hardly had Tom reached the house, it started to snow heavily.
options_map.D: Hardly had reached the house Tom, it started to snow heavily.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Hardly had Tom reached the house, it started to snow heavily.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: If 'hardly' goes in the beginning of the sentence we should invert subject and predicate. Compare: Tom had reached (normal word order) - had Tom reached (inverted order).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Do you know ____ girl who is standing next to Caroline?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'the' with all kinds of nouns when we talk about definite and specific things.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My parents ________ (to travel) since last May and they are not at home yet.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Present Perfect Continuous for actions that started in the past and continue in present. By using this tense we also emphasize the process.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Charlie ___ (to come) home before Andy ___ (to finish) cooking.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The first action (Charlie had come home) happened earlier than the second one (Andy finished cooking). To show this sequence we use Past Perfect and Past Simple one after another.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Unfortunately, the disease ________ (still / to spread) during next few months.
options: is still be going to spread

options_map.D: is still be going to spread

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Continuous Tense to show that the action is developing in the present and that we expect it to continue in the future.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active Voice sentence into the Passive one: Everyone believes that the rescue group will complete the work successfully.
options: The rescue group it is believed will complete the work successfully.
It believed that the rescue group will complete the work successfully.
It is believed that the rescue group will complete the work successfully.
It is believed that the work successfully  will complete the rescue group.

options_map.A: The rescue group it is believed will complete the work successfully.
options_map.B: It believed that the rescue group will complete the work successfully.
options_map.C: It is believed that the rescue group will complete the work successfully.
options_map.D: It is believed that the work successfully  will complete the rescue group.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: It is believed that the rescue group will complete the work successfully.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The Present Simple Passive is formed: BE + Past Participle. The correct word order is represented in answer 3.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The company ___ an interesting offer to us.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to make an offer'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Sandra always ___ (to act extra special in public) when she wears a new dress.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to show off' means 'to act extra special in public'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to spell' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO SPELL - SPELT - SPELT.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ the traffic jams, we couldn't get there on time.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Traffic jams' is the reason why we couldn't get there on time. To introduce a reason we could also use 'because'. But you should remember that after 'because' we place a clause. Linking words of reason that are followed by a noun are: owing to, due to, because of. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ friends are worse than enemies.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that the adjective 'honest' is used with the prefix 'dis-'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Peter didn't hesitate even a second. He pushed the door open ___ and went outside.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we do something 'decisively' we do not think twice. We take the decision quickly and firmly. Other options do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Brittany tried ___ (to learn) English, but she didn't succeed in it.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Some verbs can be used both with the Gerund and the Infinitive. But in some cases the meaning of the sentence becomes different. Compare: she tried eating carrot jam - she experimented with the jam, but she didn't enjoy it / she tried to learn English - she started something but didn't have success.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This task was a piece ___ cake.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'piece of'. Idiom 'to be a piece of cake' means 'to be easy to do something'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The figure skating competition is ___  now.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'to be underway'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Terry is sorry ___ being rude.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'sorry for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My little niece likes _________ very much.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are some nouns which have the same form in the singular and in the plural: FRUIT - FRUIT (if we speak about it in general). But speaking about different types - we say: KINDS OF FRUITS.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ men, ___ minds (idiom).
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'Many men, many minds'. 'Many' is used before countable nouns. 'Much' and 'a little' - before uncountable. We use 'any' in negative and interrogative sentences.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express regret about the past: We regret that we visited that museum.
options: We wish we didn't visit that museum.
We wish we hadn't visited that museum.
We wouldn't have visited that museum.

options_map.B: We wish we didn't visit that museum.
options_map.C: We wish we hadn't visited that museum.
options_map.D: We wouldn't have visited that museum.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: We wish we hadn't visited that museum.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to show regret about the past we usually use the construction [ I + wish + Past Perfect]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Form a compound adjective from two words: single + storey
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'single-storey'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Select the answer with the right word order
options: Never before such a beautiful place had  visited Jake.
Never before Jake had visited such a beautiful place.
Never before had Jake visited such a beautiful place.
Never before such a beautiful place Jake had  visited.

options_map.A: Never before such a beautiful place had  visited Jake.
options_map.B: Never before Jake had visited such a beautiful place.
options_map.C: Never before had Jake visited such a beautiful place.
options_map.D: Never before such a beautiful place Jake had  visited.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Never before had Jake visited such a beautiful place.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When a sentence starts with 'never before' subject and predicate (that go after it) are usually inverted. In spoken language it is possible to use option 2, but formally it is not correct. Other answers are illogical or wrong.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: His son plays ___ cello skillfully.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 'The' is used before names of musical instruments.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Paul ___ (to read) this book for over two months.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Present Perfect Continuous to emphasise the duration of the action.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It ________ (to happen) last year. I ________ (to swim) in the sea when unexpectedly I _________ (to see) the burning ship.
options: was happening / was swimming / was seeing

options_map.B: was happening / was swimming / was seeing

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation:
1. 'Last year' is a hint to use the Past Simple: happened. 
2. For a longer action in the past we use the Past Continuous and for a short one - the Past Simple: was swimming/saw.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: By the time Katie ___ (to leave) she ___ (to be) in Rome for a year.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to show that the action will continue up until another one in the future we use the Future Perfect.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The song 'I will always love you' ___ (to compose) by a singer Dolly Parton in 1974.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Sometimes we need to change a sentence from the Active Voice into the Passive Voice. We can also know a person who carries out the action. In this case we use the Passive Voice and form a sentence according to this rule:  Subject - Be+ Past Participle - Preposition 'BY' - Agent (who or what carries out the action). In this sentence the action took place at a certain time in the past, so we use the Past Simple Passive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I'm so tired. I need to ___ a walk in the park.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to take a walk'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ________ (to be attentive to probable risk) icicles on the roof.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to watch out for' means 'to be attentive to probable risk'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Barbara stopped ___ to text Brian.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To text Brian' is a purpose why Barbara stopped. When we introduce a purpose we use 'in order/so as + to-infinitive' or 'so (that)/in order (that) + clause'. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Oh, God! Do you see Mike? He looks ___ ridiculous in this yellow coat.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Utterly means 'extremely, totally, completely'. Other answers are not possible according to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Drew offered _______ (to have) a rest.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Offer requires the Infinitive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: In answer ___ his  letter of inquiry Bill was invited to an executive session.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'in answer to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Mary is still in the hospital. But she is  ___ high spirits.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'in high spirits'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This behaviour is very peculiar ___ Tim. He is a real rowdy.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'peculiar to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Bus is a very comfortable ________ of transport.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are some nouns which have the same form in the singular and in the plural: ONE MEANS - TWO MEANS.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It was hard but we have done ___ of the work finally. Now we have less than a half.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Many is used before countable nouns. 'Much' and 'a little' - before uncountable. 'A little' doesn't relate to the meaning. We use 'any' in interrogative and negative sentences.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If  Mike ___ (to have) time he ___ (can earn) more teaching  Polish in addition to his main work.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about imaginary situations which differ from real facts in the present we use Conditional 2: If-clause (if + Past Simple) - Main Clause (would/could + present without 'to'). The meaning of this sentence: in reality Mike doesn't have enough time to earn additional money.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a suffix to form a noun from a given word: refuge
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'refugee'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose the string with the right word order
options: Andrew bought a large beautiful round aquarium yesterday.
Andrew bought a large round beautiful aquarium yesterday.
Andrew bought a beautiful large round aquarium yesterday.
Andrew bought a round beautiful large aquarium yesterday.

options_map.A: Andrew bought a large beautiful round aquarium yesterday.
options_map.B: Andrew bought a large round beautiful aquarium yesterday.
options_map.C: Andrew bought a beautiful large round aquarium yesterday.
options_map.D: Andrew bought a round beautiful large aquarium yesterday.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Andrew bought a beautiful large round aquarium yesterday.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we need to use many adjectives in one sentence, they should be placed in the following order: Opinion - Size - Age - Shape - Colour - Origin - Material. 'Beautiful' is an opinion adjective, 'large' is an adjective of size, 'round' - an adjective that determines shape.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Brianna is ___ gifted artist. We should visit her personal exhibition.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use articles 'a/an' when we talk about jobs.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This music group_______(to become) more  and more popular. It's interesting to visit their show.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: In this sentence we are talking about developing situation.  So, in this case we should use the Present Continuous Tense. This Tense is formed: Auxiliary (am/is/are) + Verb-ing.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question:
- I ___ (to wait) for your call for hours! 
- Sorry, I ___ (to watch) TV from 7 till 10 o'clock last night and simply  ___ (to forget) to call you.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1, 2. We use the Past Continuous to show that some action was in progress at a certain time in the past - was watching TV from 7 till 10 o'clock. 3. We use the Past Simple for actions which were finished in the past - forgot.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: By next October, Jill ________ (to receive) her drivers's license.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Perfect to show that something will happen before a certain time in the future.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active Voice sentence into the Passive one: Everyone expects him to win the race.
options: He expects to win the race.
He is expected to win the race.
He has been expected to win the race.
He had been expected to win the race.

options_map.A: He expects to win the race.
options_map.B: He is expected to win the race.
options_map.C: He has been expected to win the race.
options_map.D: He had been expected to win the race.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: He is expected to win the race.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The construction [subject + passive + to-infinitive] is used to talk about people's opinions in general and to report an event. As the active sentence was formed with the Present Simple, we use the same tense in the passive one: [is/are + Past Participle].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ (to become calm, quiet and cool off) and tell me what’s happened?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to quiet down' means 'to become calm, quiet and cool off'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose two forms of the verb 'to shine' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO SHINE - SHONE - SHONE.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The red car is ________ more expensive than the black one.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We can use mitigators 'slightly, rather, a bit, a little bit' with comparative adjectives.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The problem is ___ serious.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Obviously means 'clearly understood to everyone'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Carla considered ___ (to change) her job.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Consider requires the Gerund. In this case the Gerund is used as the object of the verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We hope there will be an increase ____ salary soon.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'increase in'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Llama belongs ___ the camel family.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'to belong to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It is typical ___ her to wear far-out clothes.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'typical of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Carl lives in Sydney. He is a _______ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Sydney (city) - Sydney-sider (a person who lives in Sydney)

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: There was hardly ___ policeman on the road.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'any' in questions and negative sentences. 'Hardly' refers to the negative meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If I ______(to win) the lottery I _____(to give) all the money to charity.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about probable situations in the present or future we use Conditional 1: If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future/modal + present without 'to').

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Find the correct word formation chain (noun - adjective - verb): admiration
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'admirer - admiring - admire'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Determine the sentence with the right word order?
options: Monthly bonus it is unfair to give him.
It is unfair to give him monthly bonus again.
It is unfair him monthly bonus again to give.
To give him monthly bonus again is it unfair.

options_map.A: Monthly bonus it is unfair to give him.
options_map.B: It is unfair to give him monthly bonus again.
options_map.C: It is unfair him monthly bonus again to give.
options_map.D: To give him monthly bonus again is it unfair.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: It is unfair to give him monthly bonus again.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: In order to avoid long complex subject sentences we usually use such a structure: [it + be + noun/ adjective + to-infinitive].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Let's visit ___ Philippines next summer.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 'The' is used before the names of countries in a plural form.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Helga ________ (already / to write) an essay and she __________ (it / to check out) for two hours. Don't interrupt her.
options: has already been writing / has been checking it out
already writes / is checking it out
has already written / has checked it out
has already written / has been checking it out

options_map.A: has already been writing / has been checking it out
options_map.B: already writes / is checking it out
options_map.C: has already written / has checked it out
options_map.D: has already written / has been checking it out

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: has already written / has been checking it out
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. 'Already' shows us that the action is complete and we see the result in the present. This is why the Present Perfect is an appropriate tense for the first part of the sentence. 2. 'For two hours' and 'Don't interrupt her' shows that the process (has been checking it out) is still in progress. It started in the past and continues up in the present, therefore we use the Present Perfect Continuous.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Julia ___ (to take) a leash and ___ (to go) out to walk her dog in the park.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we talk about actions which happened one after the other in the past we use the Past Simple Tense.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Teresa ___ (to see) her son's teacher tomorrow morning.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: If we have decided to do something or arranged to do something in the near future we use 'be going to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active Voice sentence into the Passive one: Someone turned the light off.
options: The light was turned someone off.

options_map.D: The light was turned someone off.

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: If there is a particle or a preposition after a verb in the Active Voice sentence than we do not omit it in the Passive one. The correct word order is represented in answer 2.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Do not eat junk food ____ hamburgers and fizzy drinks.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to say 'for example' we can use 'like'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ (to visit informally, to look in), if you visit Munich! I'm always glad to see you.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to drop in' means 'to visit informally, to look in'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to stink' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO STINK - STANK - STUNK

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Bobby can stay here _______ he keeps quiet.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to express a condition we usually use these linking words: as long as, provided/providing (that).  Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Barbara is so __________ . She thinks that she is the best and doesn't pay attention to anyone around her.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Arrogant means 'having too much sense of self-importance'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ , we have lost the game and it's only our fault. I've got nothing to add.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Anyway is the only logically correct adverb for the sentence. We use it to show that the conversation is about to finish. By using it we return to the main idea and sum it up.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Tracey forgot ___ (to lock) the door. She spent the day trying to remember that fact. So she called her neighbour to ask him to check the door.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Some verbs can be used both with the Gerund and the Infinitive. But in some cases the meaning of the sentence becomes different. Compare: forgot to lock - forgot that she needed to lock / forgot locking - she locked the door but she forgot that fact.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Teachers of this high school place emphasis ____ practical work.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'emphasis on'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Look! The helicopter is flying ____ us.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'to fly over something/somebody'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Leo is eager ___ fame since childhood.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'eager for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This is ___. My congratulations!
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are some nouns which are used only in a plural form: NEWS - NEWS.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Do you know Mr. Dickens? - Yes, I do, but I can't say ___ bad about him. He's so secretive.
