multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the pronoun 'something' to refer to things in affirmative sentences, while 'anything' — in interrogative and negative ones. 'Any' and 'some' are pronouns which don't relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If Tom ___ (to lead) a healthy life, he ___ (not to suffer) from pressure-surge problems.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about imaginary situations which differ from real facts in the present we use Conditional 2: If-clause (if + Past Simple) - Main Clause (would/could + present without 'to'). The meaning of this sentence: in reality Tom doesn't lead healthy life so he suffers  from pressure-surge problems.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Find the correct word formation chain (noun - adjective - verb): addiction
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'addict - addictive - to become addicted'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Determine the sentence with the right word order:
options: I didn't like new haircut her.
Her new haircut like I didn't.
I didn't her new haircut like.
Her new haircut I didn't like.

options_map.A: I didn't like new haircut her.
options_map.B: Her new haircut like I didn't.
options_map.C: I didn't her new haircut like.
options_map.D: Her new haircut I didn't like.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Her new haircut I didn't like.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We can move the object to the beginning of the sentence in order to place emphasis on the certain point or idea. Here it was important for  the speaker to express his reaction to the haircut, not something else.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ Moon goes around ___ Earth once every twenty eight days.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 'The' is used before nouns which are unique.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I _____ (to try) to wake up at 8 o'clock every morning, but today I ______ (to oversleep). Now I ______ (to make) up leeway.
options: have tried / have overslept / am making

options_map.B: have tried / have overslept / am making

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation:
1. 'Every morning' is a mark that shows us that the action is regular. So we choose the Present Simple.
2. 'Today' shows us that the time period is not over, so we choose the Present Perfect.
3. 'Now' shows that the process is developing at the moment, that is why we choose the Present Continuous.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Kimberly's parents ___ (to divorce) when she ___ (to be) sixteen years old.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Past Simple Tense when we talk about actions which happened at a certain time in the past.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Sandra ___ (to work) for five years for this company in October.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Perfect Continuous to concentrate on the duration of the action which may continue after the mentioned time point. Here: Sandra will probably work for the company after October. And in October she will celebrate her 5 year employee anniversary.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This part of the road  ____(to repair) in three weeks.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we don't know who carries out the action, or it is obvious or unimportant to us, we use the Passive voice. In this sentence we speak about the action which will be completed in the future: Will Be + Past Participle.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It is difficult but I have to ___ a decision.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to make a decision' or 'to take a decision'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Paris ___ (to forget) Matt's name ___ when she made a wedding guest list.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to leave out' means 'to fail to mention, to forget'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose two forms of the verb 'to speed' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO SPEED - SPED - SPED.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: _________ Andy Murray showed a massive dominance in the first two sets, he surprisingly lost the whole game.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to show a conflict between the main clause and the statement in the subordinate clause we can use 'although (and its synonyms), while, whilst or whereas'. Note that 'while' and 'whilst' are used mostly in formal contexts. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The journalist called the party's election tactics _______ . But unfortunately many voters trusted it.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Deceitful means 'dishonest. Someone who tries to make everyone believe in what is not true'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The summer is coming, so it’s important to know how to get tanned ___ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Safely means 'free from harm or danger'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I think the team really deserves ___ (to win) the game.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 'Deserve' requires the Infinitive. We cannot use the Gerund with this verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I  feel a need ___ some changes in life.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To be in need of something, but to have/feel a need for something.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: He got married ___ the age ___ 35.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'at the age of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Mrs. Whirpool is always nice ___ us.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'nice to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: His scientific study is called 'Rare _________ (plural of phenomenon) of nature'.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The noun 'phenomenon' has the irregular plural form: PHENOMENON - PHENOMENA

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I haven't seen my elder sister for ___ years.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Many is used before plural countable nouns. 'Little' and 'much' - before uncountable nouns. 'Every' doesn't relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express disappointment with the present situation: Nigel has to get up early every morning. He doesn't like it.
options: Nigel wishes he didn't have to get up early every morning.
Nigel would get up early every morning if he liked it.
If only Nigel got up early every morning he would like it.
Nigel would like to get up early every morning if he had to.

options_map.A: Nigel wishes he didn't have to get up early every morning.
options_map.B: Nigel would get up early every morning if he liked it.
options_map.C: If only Nigel got up early every morning he would like it.
options_map.D: Nigel would like to get up early every morning if he had to.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Nigel wishes he didn't have to get up early every morning.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To express disappointment with the present situation we usually use the construction [ I + wish + Past Simple]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a prefix to make a word negative: perfect
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'perfect - imperfect'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Opt the sentence with the right word order?
options: My uncle is a tall dark-eyed middle-aged  man.
My uncle is a dark-eyed tall middle-aged  man.
My uncle is a middle-aged tall dark-eyed man.
My uncle is a tall middle-aged dark-eyed man.

options_map.A: My uncle is a tall dark-eyed middle-aged  man.
options_map.B: My uncle is a dark-eyed tall middle-aged  man.
options_map.C: My uncle is a middle-aged tall dark-eyed man.
options_map.D: My uncle is a tall middle-aged dark-eyed man.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: My uncle is a tall middle-aged dark-eyed man.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There is a certain word order in statements with the Past Simple Tense: Subject - Verb - Object. When we need to use many adjectives in one sentence, they should be placed in the following order: Opinion - Size - Age - Shape - Colour - Origin - Material. 'Tall' is a size, 'middle-aged' - the age and 'dark-eyed' - the colour.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: _______ Himalayas, which are situated in South Asia, is one of the longest mountain ranges in the world.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'the' before mountain ranges.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: She ____ (to be) a nice girl. But now she _____ (to be) so rude.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. We use the Present Simple to talk about things in general, common regular situations and behaviour. 2. Some state verbs can be used in continuous form with the change of meaning: 'she is nice' is a personal characteristic / 'she is being rude' is her behaviour at the moment.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: When I ______ (to come) home I _______ (to see) nobody. It ______ (to seem) like everyone _______ (to go) not less than an hour before.
options: had come / had seen / seemed / had gone
was coming / saw / had seemed / had gone

options_map.B: had come / had seen / seemed / had gone
options_map.D: was coming / saw / had seemed / had gone

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Past Simple Tense when we talk about actions which happened one after the other in the past: came - saw - seemed. 'Before' shows us that the last action happened some time earlier than actions in the first part. The Past Perfect helps us carry out this idea.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My luggage is too heavy. ___ (to help / you) me, please?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Simple Tense in requests.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active Voice sentence into the Passive one: Romans used the Colloseum for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.
options: The Colloseum used to be for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.
The Colloseum used for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.
The Colloseum had been used for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.
The Colloseum was used for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.

options_map.A: The Colloseum used to be for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.
options_map.B: The Colloseum used for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.
options_map.C: The Colloseum had been used for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.
options_map.D: The Colloseum was used for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: The Colloseum was used for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The correct form of the Past Simple Passive is performed in the answer 4. This tense is used for complete actions in the past.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The team used a big tree ___ a shelter.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we describe how we use something we take 'as'. 'Like' means 'similar to something'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Hey you, Bart! Quit ______(to laze) and help me repair the gate!
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to goof off' means 'do careless work, to laze'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to arise' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO ARISE - AROSE - ARISEN

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: _________ the weather forecasts the city was hit by huge snowstorm.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to show there is a surprising contrast between two statements in one sentence we use 'although, though, even though' and 'despite/in spite of + -ing/noun/pronoun'. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Alison plaited her ___ hair.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There is a certain word order in sentences with two or more adjectives: OPINION-SIZE-AGE-SHAPE-COLOUR-ORIGIN-MATERIAL-TYPE. Here: long (size) wavy (shape) red (colour) hair.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Fred broke a porcelain vase __.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use adverbs to describe time, degree, manner, etc. In other words adverbs help us get more information about the action or a place (where, when, how, how often, etc.) They are formed by adding '-ly' or '-ily' to the adjective. Some forms should be memorized: accidentally.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: He refused ___ (to tell) me the truth.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 'Refuse' requires the Infinitive. We cannot use the Gerund with this verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Do you know that water pollution is one of offences ___ the environment and that it is punished by law?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'offence against'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My brother graduated ___ the university two years ago.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'to graduate from'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Leo is excellent ___ playing chess.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'excellent at'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Akash lives in New Delhi. He is a ___ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: New Delhi (city) - Delhiite (a person who lives in New Delhi)

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Tara doesn’t speak French well. She knows only ___ expressions.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: A few is used before countable nouns. 'A little' - before uncountable nouns. 'Many' and 'a lot of' do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express the idea when you want someone to do something in the present or future: I don't want you to to meet him anymore.
options: I'd rather you hadn't met him anymore.
I'd rather you didn't meet him anymore.
I wish you met him anymore.
I wish you hadn't met him anymore.

options_map.A: I'd rather you hadn't met him anymore.
options_map.B: I'd rather you didn't meet him anymore.
options_map.C: I wish you met him anymore.
options_map.D: I wish you hadn't met him anymore.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: I'd rather you didn't meet him anymore.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we need to express the idea when you want someone to do something in the present or future we usually use the construction [would rather + subject + Past Simple]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a suffix to form an adjective from a given word: worth
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'worthless'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Opt the sentence with the right word order:
options: What the results are of your blood test?
What are the results of your blood test?
What the results of your blood test are?
What of your blood test are the results?

options_map.A: What the results are of your blood test?
options_map.B: What are the results of your blood test?
options_map.C: What the results of your blood test are?
options_map.D: What of your blood test are the results?

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: What are the results of your blood test?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we ask a Wh-question we use the following word order: Question Word - Auxiliary - Subject - Object. 'What' is a question word, 'are' - an auxiliary verb, 'the results' - a subject, 'of your blood test' - an object.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I got up early in ___ morning.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The is used before the words 'evening/night/morning/afternoon'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Claire _______ (to travel) to Spain last year but she _______ (never / to be) to Portugal.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. 'Last year' shows us that the action was complete in the past, therefore we use the Past Simple. 2. We use the Present Perfect for actions which started in the past and continue up to the present. She has never travelled to Portugal - it means that she didn't visit that country in the past and this situation is still actual for the present.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: As soon as Jake _______ (to answer), he ________ (to realize) his mistake.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Past Perfect to show that one action happened before the second one. Here: at first he had answered and after that he realized that he had made a mistake.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jim's parents ___ (to buy) a car tomorrow. They have already chosen it.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Present Continuous to talk about future plans which have already been arranged.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active Voice sentence into the Passive one: Millions of people around the world have already read this book.
options: This book was already been read by millions of people around the world.
Millions of people around the world  has already been read by this book.
This book has already read by millions of people around the world.
This book has already been read by millions of people around the world.

options_map.A: This book was already been read by millions of people around the world.
options_map.B: Millions of people around the world  has already been read by this book.
options_map.C: This book has already read by millions of people around the world.
options_map.D: This book has already been read by millions of people around the world.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: This book has already been read by millions of people around the world.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Sometimes we need to change a sentence from the Active Voice into the Passive Voice. We can also know a person who carries out the action. In this case we use the Passive Voice and form a sentence according to this rule:  Subject - Be + Past Participle - Preposition 'BY' - Agent (who or what carries out the action). In this sentence we use the Present Perfect Passive: has been read.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Rick tries to _____ his best at work.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to do best'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We have already been discussing the problem for 3 hours. I think it is time to _____ (to finish) our conference.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to wrap up' means 'to complete, finish'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to mow' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To mow - mowed - mown.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Fierce hurricane has destroyed dozens of buildings in the town. _______ Sam's family has to find another place to live.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we talk about a result we use 'so, therefore, as a result, for this reason'. Notice that they are usually come at the beginning of the sentence but it is possible for 'so' and ' therefore' to take also a middle position. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: To achieve success, we need to find the most ________ way to solve the problem.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The adjective 'effective' means 'successful in achieving a desired result.'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This politician is not a person who speaks ________ about the real economic situation in the country.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The adverb 'truthfully' means that someone speaks honestly.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Justin imagines ___ (to live) in London one day.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Imagine requires the Gerund. In this case the Gerund is used as the object of the verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Charlie is an optimist. He always tries to make use ___ even unpleasant situations in his life.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'use of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Ben is going to travel ___ China from May ___  July.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'through China' and 'from May through July'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Mr. Brooks is thankful ___ the yearly Managers' Award.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'thankful for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The american F-22 Raptor air superiority fighter is one of the world's most powerful ___ nowadays.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are some nouns which have the same form in the singular and in the plural: AIRCRAFT - AIRCRAFT.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Tim celebrates his 21st birthday in ten days. Do you have ___ gift idea?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Many is used before countable nouns. 'Much' and 'a little' - before uncountable. We use 'any' in interrogative and negative sentences.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If Sandra ___ (to take) a painkiller, she ___ (to feel) better soon.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about probable situations in the present or future we use Conditional 1: If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future/modal + present without 'to').

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Find the correct word formation chain (noun - adjective - verb): achievement
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'achiever - achieved - achieve'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Pick out the sentence with the right word order?
options: I'm a bit late, am not I?
I'm, aren't I, a bit late?
Aren't I, I'm a bit late?
I'm a bit late, aren't I?

options_map.A: I'm a bit late, am not I?
options_map.B: I'm, aren't I, a bit late?
options_map.C: Aren't I, I'm a bit late?
options_map.D: I'm a bit late, aren't I?

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: I'm a bit late, aren't I?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We place tag questions in the end of the sentence after a comma. The tag question always starts with the auxiliary verb: aren't I? It is correct to say [aren't I] not [am not I]

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The Smiths went to ____ Alps to ski.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The is used before names of groups of islands, states, mountain chains.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: In his essay, professor Nickson ___ (to admit) the existance of UFO, but ___ (to point) out the fact that we still ___ (to have) no proved evidence of their existence.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The best suitable tense for this sentence is the Present Simple. It is often used when we give some kind of a review or a summary. For example, it can be a book, a movie, a theatre play, etc.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: By the time he ___ (to get) home, she ___ (to play) the piano for 3 hours.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. We use the Past Simple for short complete actions in the past - he got home. 2. We often use the Past Perfect Continuous to emphasize the duration of the action which started in the past and continued up to the specific time in the past - she had been playing before he came and continued playing after.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Call me at 10 o'clock tomorrow, OK? - Sorry, I won't be able to call you. I ______ (to jog).
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Continuous to emphasize that the action will be in progress at the certain time point in the future.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active voice sentence to the Passive one: They clean my car once a week.
options: I have cleaned my car once a week.
I get my car cleaned once a week.
I get my car cleaning once a week.
My car have been cleaned once a week by them.

options_map.A: I have cleaned my car once a week.
options_map.B: I get my car cleaned once a week.
options_map.C: I get my car cleaning once a week.
options_map.D: My car have been cleaned once a week by them.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: I get my car cleaned once a week.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Passive Causative to talk about services that will be done or were done for us by someone else. We form the Passive Causative with the help of two structures: [have / get + something + past participle]. According to grammar it would be correct to use answer 4, but in spoken language it's mostly common to use the Passive Causative form.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This article will tell how to make your ___ around the world cheaper.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Voyage - is a long trip, very often at sea. 'Journey' - means moving from one point to another in a vehicle (bus journey, train journey, etc.). Trip - covers the whole process (moving somewhere and back, rest, pleasure and purpose). 'Travel' - is used to talk about the activity of moving from one point to another generally (air travels has become more expensive this year)

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My boss wants me ___ the report ___ (to do something again). The first one was too short and illogical as he said.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to do over' means 'to do something again'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to slay' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO SLAY - SLEW - SLAIN.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We decided to stay at home, _________ the bad weather.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The bad weather is the reason why we decided to stay at home. To introduce a reason we could use 'because' and 'because of'. But you should remember that after 'because' we place a clause. Linking words of reason that are followed by a noun are: owing to, due to, because of. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I like his _______ way of thinking. He always plans everything in advance and never forgets anything.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Prudent means 'reasonable, arranged, thinking about the future'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Your dress goes ___ with these shoes.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Elegantly means 'in a graceful, beautiful and nice manner'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Father resisted _______ (to ask) for help.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Resist requires the Gerund. In this case the Gerund is used as the object of the verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Vanessa failed the entrance exam. I feel pity ___ her.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'pity for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My friends left 3 hours ago and they should have arrived ___ now.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'by now' speaking about a deadline, time-limit.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Give me a pair of _______ , please.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The noun 'scissors' is just used in a plural form: SCISSORS - SCISSORS.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Would you like an apple or a banana? - It doesn't matter, ______ is good for me.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Either is used to express a similarity with a statement made. Here: you can give an apple or a banana because I like them both.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If I ___________ (to be) Fred I _________ (to think) several times before making such a tattoo.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about imaginary situations which differ from real facts in the present we use Conditional 2: If-clause (if + Past Simple) - Main Clause (would/could + present without 'to'). The meaning of this sentence: in reality Fred made a very strange tattoo.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Form a compound adjective from two words: brand + new
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'brand-new'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Pick out the sentence with the right word order:
options: They took a kitten small black  home.
They took a small black  kitten home.
They took a  black  small kitten home.
Home they took home a  black  small kitten.

options_map.A: They took a kitten small black  home.
options_map.B: They took a small black  kitten home.
options_map.C: They took a  black  small kitten home.
options_map.D: Home they took home a  black  small kitten.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: They took a small black  kitten home.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There is a certain word order in statements: Subject - Verb - Object. When we need to use many adjectives in one sentence, they should be placed in the following order: Opinion - Size - Age - Shape - Colour - Origin - Material. 'Small' is a characteristic of size and 'black' - is a characteristic of colour.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The Mona Lisa is ___  real masterpiece.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the article 'a' with singular countable nouns when we talk about them in general. 'An' is used before words starting with sounds [a], [e], [i], [o], [u].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: When I ___ (to quarrel) with my sister she just ___ (to stop) talking to me. She ___ (always / to ignore) me!
options: has quarrelled / has stopped / always ignores
am quarrelling / stops / has always ignored
quarrel / has stopped / is always ignoring

options_map.A: has quarrelled / has stopped / always ignores
options_map.B: am quarrelling / stops / has always ignored
options_map.C: quarrel / has stopped / is always ignoring

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. When we talk about common, regular situations in the present we use the Present Simple: we quarrel, she stops. 2. We often use the Present Continuous to express our negative attitude to a situation: she's always ignoring me!

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jake ______ (to come) home totally exhausted. He _______ (to drive) all day long.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. We use the Past Simple for short complete actions in the past - he came home. 2. The most appropriate tense for the second part is, the Past Perfect Continuous - because we certainly want to emphasize the process, not the result.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I believe that our team _____(to take) the first place in a volleyball championship tomorrow.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Simple Tense when we make predictions, talk about desires and hopes connected with the future.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active voice sentence to the Passive one: Someone did it for me yesterday.
options: It had been done for me by someone yesterday.
Someone had been done for me by it yesterday.

options_map.C: It had been done for me by someone yesterday.
options_map.D: Someone had been done for me by it yesterday.

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Passive Causative to talk about services that will be done or were done for us by someone else. We form the Passive Causative with the help of two structures: [have / get + something + past participle]. According to grammar it would be correct to use answer 3, but in everyday language it's mostly common to use the Passive Causative form. Then, answer 1 has another meaning. Compare: I had it done - someone did it for me / I had done it - I did it myself.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Honey, you are ill. ______ a medicine, please.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to take a medicine'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I _____ (to cancel) my Sunday walk in the park because of the oncoming frost.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to call off' means 'to cancel, delay'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to redo' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO REDO - REDID - REDONE.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We made a decision to apply to the court ___ to get a refund from the online store.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To get a refund from the online store is a purpose why we took a decision to apply to the court. When we introduce a purpose we use 'in order/so as + to-infinitive' or 'so (that)/in order (that) + clause'. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I respect Mr. Smith for his ___ point of view.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Impartial means 'objective'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Look! It's raining _____. Stay overnight at our place.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we talk about rain we use 'heavily'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Bart tends ___ (to be) very mean.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Tend requires the Infinitive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Darwin’s Theory of Evolution  made a great impact ___ the development of biology.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'impact on'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Don't be so mean ____ your brother.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'mean to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Police officers march to honor their fallen ___ throughout the country.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The noun 'brother' in the meaning 'a fellow member' (of any party, sect, society etc) has the irregular plural form: BROTHER - BRETHREN.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Look! I have brought ____ for you!
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the pronoun 'something' to refer to things in affirmative sentences, while 'anything'  and 'nothing' - in negative ones. 'Some' is a pronoun that doesn't relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If I ___ (to find) this book, I ___ (to buy) it for you.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about probable situations in the present or future we use Conditional 1: If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future / modal + present without 'to').

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a suffix to form a noun from a given word: advertise
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'advertisement'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Pick the sentence with the right word order?
options: Can Mr. Johnson be soon given a new car?
Can soon Mr. Johnson be given a new car?
Can Mr. Johnson soon be given a new car?
Can a new car Mr. Johnson soon be given?

options_map.A: Can Mr. Johnson be soon given a new car?
options_map.B: Can soon Mr. Johnson be given a new car?
options_map.C: Can Mr. Johnson soon be given a new car?
options_map.D: Can a new car Mr. Johnson soon be given?

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Can Mr. Johnson soon be given a new car?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we ask a question with the modal verb we place the modal in the beginning: [MODAL + SUBJECT + MAIN VERB + OBJECT]. Adverbs like «soon, yet, usually» are placed between the subject and the root verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Kara is majoring in ___ Chemistry and ___ Physics.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We do not use articles before school or academic subjects.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The next bus _________ (to leave) at 7 p.m., but I _______ still (not to buy) a ticket!
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. We use the Present Simple to talk about scheduled events and habitual actions. 2. We use «still» to refer to unfinished actions, especially when we expected to finish them earlier. The Present Perfect expresses this idea completely.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: That red car ________ (to belong) to Jim for 3 years before he _______ (to sell) it.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. According to the meaning it would be correct to use the Past Perfect Continuous for the first part because it is obviously important for the speaker to emphasize the duration of the process here: for 3 years. But we remember that non-continuous verbs cannot be used with '-ing'. So it is correct to choose the Past Perfect Tense. 2. We use the Past Simple for completed actions in the past.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jessica ___ (to study) for 6 years when she finally graduates.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The Future Perfect Continuous (like the Future Perfect) expresses the idea that an action will continue up until another one or certain time point in the Future. But the Future Perfect Continuous is more concentrated on the duration. We use it when it is important for us to emphasise 'how long' something will be in progress in the future: for an hour, for a week, for a year, etc.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active voice sentence to the Passive one: this company will mow the lawn for our neighbours tomorrow.
options: Our neighbours will be mowed their lawn tomorrow.
Our neighbours will mow their lawn tomorrow.
Our neighbours will have their lawn mowed tomorrow.
This company will have their lawn mowed by our neighbours tomorrow.

options_map.A: Our neighbours will be mowed their lawn tomorrow.
options_map.B: Our neighbours will mow their lawn tomorrow.
options_map.C: Our neighbours will have their lawn mowed tomorrow.
options_map.D: This company will have their lawn mowed by our neighbours tomorrow.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Our neighbours will have their lawn mowed tomorrow.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Causative Passive to say that some service was done / will be done for us by someone else. It's formed: [subject + causative verb + object + past participle].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Barry will stay at home for a while. He has ___ the flu.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to get the flu'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The fire ___ (to begin) in a two-storey building which we had been living in before.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use phrasal verb 'to break out' when something dangerous and potentially harmful suddenly begins.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to shed' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO SHED -  SHED - SHED.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ Mark was going to find a new job, he decided to learn French to get a higher position.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Mark was going to find a new job is the reason why he decided to learn French. To give a reason for a certain situation we use 'seeing that, seeing as, as, because, since' + clause. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Mr. Freeman works in a ___ (medical/famous/German) school.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There is a certain word order in sentences with two or more adjectives: OPINION-SIZE-AGE-SHAPE-COLOUR-ORIGIN-MATERIAL-TYPE. Here: a famous (opinion) German (origin) medical (type) school.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The vase was very fragile. Garry placed it down on the table ___ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Gingerly means 'carefully'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My neighbor practices _______ (to play) the guitar every day.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Practice requires the Gerund. In this case the Gerund is used as the object of the verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Titanic is ____ far the most touching movie I've ever watched.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'by far' in the meaning of 'undoubtedly'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Never be jealous ___ someone's success. You never know it's price.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'jealous of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: John lives in Cape Town. He is a _______ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Cape Town (city) - Capetonian (a person who lives in Cape Town)

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Are there ___ amusement parks in the city?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'any' in interrogative and negative sentences. 'A lot of' and 'much' do not relate to the meaning of the sentence. 'Some' is not usually used in questions.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express disappointment with the present situation: Sarah has to work 6 days a week. She doesn't like it.
options: Sarah would work 6 days a week if she liked it.
Sarah wishes she didn't have to work 6 days a week.
If only Sarah had to work 6 days a week.
Sarah would work 6 days a week if she had to.

options_map.A: Sarah would work 6 days a week if she liked it.
options_map.B: Sarah wishes she didn't have to work 6 days a week.
options_map.C: If only Sarah had to work 6 days a week.
options_map.D: Sarah would work 6 days a week if she had to.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Sarah wishes she didn't have to work 6 days a week.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To express disappointment with the present situation we usually use the construction [ I + wish + Past Simple]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a prefix to make a word negative: legibility
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'legibility - illegibility'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Pick the sentence with the right word order:
options: Darrel ran his schoolmate in the mall into.
Darrel ran his schoolmate into in the mall.

Darrel into ran his schoolmate in the mall.

options_map.B: Darrel ran his schoolmate into in the mall.
options_map.C: Darrel ran into his schoolmate in the mall.
options_map.D: Darrel into ran his schoolmate in the mall.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Darrel ran into his schoolmate in the mall.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we use phrasal verbs we should remember that some of them are separable while others cannot be separated. 'To run into' belongs to inseparable phrasal verbs.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Drake is going to move to ___ Republic of Ireland.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The is used before the names of countries with 'republic', 'kingdom', 'states'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The Queen of Great Britain ___ (to live) in Buckingham Palace. I ___ (never / to see) it but I ___ (always / to dream) about it.
options: is living / have never seen / have always dreamt
lives / have never seen / have always dreamt
lives / have never seen / I'm always dreaming
lives / never saw / have always dreamt

options_map.A: is living / have never seen / have always dreamt
options_map.B: lives / have never seen / have always dreamt
options_map.C: lives / have never seen / I'm always dreaming
options_map.D: lives / never saw / have always dreamt

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: lives / have never seen / have always dreamt
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. We use the Present Simple to talk about facts and things that are generally true - we all know that the Queen of England lives in Buckingham Palace. 2. We use the Present Perfect to talk about actions that started in the past and have the connection with the moment of speaking: I didn't see the Palace in the past and still dream about it in the present.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: He ___ (to enter) the kitchen, ___ (to drink) a glass of juice and ___ (to turn) on the TV.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we talk about actions which happened one after the other in the past we use the Past Simple Tense.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I'm hungry. - Well, I ___ (to order) a pizza for you.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Simple Tense when we have no plan or decision before we speak. We make it at the time of speaking.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active voice sentence to the Passive one: The Simpsanes ordered to repair their house after a devastating flood.
options: The Simpsanes had their house been repaired after a devastating flood.
The Simpsanes had their house repaired after a devastating flood.
The Simpsanes had repaired  their house after a devastating flood.
The Simpsanes had their house been repairing after a devastating flood.

options_map.A: The Simpsanes had their house been repaired after a devastating flood.
options_map.B: The Simpsanes had their house repaired after a devastating flood.
options_map.C: The Simpsanes had repaired  their house after a devastating flood.
options_map.D: The Simpsanes had their house been repairing after a devastating flood.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: The Simpsanes had their house repaired after a devastating flood.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Causative Passive to say that some service was done / will be done for us by someone else. It is formed: [subject + causative verb + object + past participle].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The troupe is ___ the performance tonight.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to give a performance'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Matt has ___ (to disappoint / me). He failed to keep his word.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to let down' means 'to disappoint'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose two forms of the verb 'to cast' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO CAST - CAST - CAST.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Maria's summary report is ____ (detailed) than Ted's one.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we compare two things or two people we use the comparative form of adjectives. If we have a long adjective (with two or more syllables), we add 'more' before it.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I ___ hope that he will be alright soon.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Sincerely means 'genuinely, honestly and truly'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Brittany tried ___ (to eat) the carrot jam once, but she didn't like it.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Some verbs can be used both with the Gerund and the Infinitive. But in some cases the meaning of the sentence becomes different. Compare: she tried eating carrot jam - she experimented with the jam, but she didn't enjoy it / she tried to learn English - she started but didn't succeed.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Our executive director warned us about a possible reduction ___ staff.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'reduction in'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: _______ the difference in their ages Nina and Den are very happy with each other.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'despite'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I like to be surrounded ___ energetic and open-hearted people.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'surrounded by'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We don't have enough ___ in our office
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The noun 'postman' has the irregular plural form: POSTMAN - POSTMEN.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We may not finish repairs in time. We need ___ extra hands.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'some' in positive sentences and 'any' in negative ones before countable or uncountable nouns. 'Much' and 'a little' are used before  uncountable nouns.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express regret about the past: Jacob regrets that he bought that car.

Jacob wishes he hadn't bought that car.
Jacob wouldn't have bought that car.

options_map.A: Jacob wishes he didn't buy that car.
options_map.B: Jacob wishes he hadn't bought that car.
options_map.D: Jacob wouldn't have bought that car.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Jacob wishes he hadn't bought that car.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to show regret about the past we usually use the construction [ I + wish + Past Perfect]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a suffix to form an adjective from a given word: accident
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'accidental'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Select the sentence with the right word order?
options: Our boss is ill, so Jack is currently filling in for him.
Our boss is ill, so Jack is currently filling for him in.

options_map.B: Our boss is ill, so Jack is currently filling for him in.
options_map.C: Our boss is ill, so Jack is currently filling him in for.
options_map.D: Our boss is ill, so Jack is currently him filling in for.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Our boss is ill, so Jack is currently filling in for him.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we use phrasal verbs we should remember that some of them are separable while others cannot be separated. 'to fill in for someone' belongs to inseparable phrasal verbs.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Sport plays ___ valuable role in my life.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the article 'a' to refer to a sample of something.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It's 10 a.m. Jake _______ (already / to have) four cups of coffee this morning. Poor thing, he _______ (to work) all night long.
options: has already had / has been working
had already had / had been working
has already had / had been working

options_map.A: has already had / has been working
options_map.C: had already had / had been working
options_map.D: has already had / had been working

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: has already had / had been working
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. We use the Present Perfect for actions which happened in an unfinished period of time - this morning. 2. We use the Past Perfect Continuous to emphasize the duration of an action which was finished in the past.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Darrel ___ (to decide) on a career of a software developer when he ___ (to be) twenty four. It ___ (not / to be) difficult because he ___ (to graduate) from IT college before.
options: decided / was / wasn't / had been graduating
decided / had been / wasn't / had graduated
decided / was / hadn't been / had graduated

options_map.A: decided / was / wasn't / had been graduating
options_map.B: decided / had been / wasn't / had graduated
options_map.D: decided / was / hadn't been / had graduated

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. We use the Past Simple for short actions in the past and actions which happened in a completed period of time: decided / was 24 / was difficult. 2. We use the Past Perfect to show that one action happened before another one: first he had graduated from the college and then he decided on a career.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I suppose that Mary ___ (to quit) the project soon.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'be going' and 'will' for guesses and predictions.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active voice sentence to the Passive one: Workers installed an air conditioning system at Jeremy's house 3 days ago.
options: Jeremy installed his home air conditioning system  3 days ago.
Jeremy had his home air conditioning system installed 3 days ago.
Jeremy had his home air conditioning system been installed 3 days ago.
Jeremy had his home air conditioning system had installed 3 days ago.

options_map.A: Jeremy installed his home air conditioning system  3 days ago.
options_map.B: Jeremy had his home air conditioning system installed 3 days ago.
options_map.C: Jeremy had his home air conditioning system been installed 3 days ago.
options_map.D: Jeremy had his home air conditioning system had installed 3 days ago.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Jeremy had his home air conditioning system installed 3 days ago.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Causative Passive to say that some service was done / will be done for us by someone else. It is formed: [subject + causative verb + object + past participle].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: British scientists have finally ___ important research.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to do research'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Patrick was so loud and noisy in the morning that I had to get up and ___ (to criticize somebody angrily).
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to chew out'  means 'to criticize somebody angrily' and 'to rebuke someone severely'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to  wring' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO WRING - WRUNG - WRUNG.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The video of the accident was ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Dreadful means 'terrible, shocking, awful'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Tom behaved ___ because he knew nobody of that company. It was difficult for him to start a conversation.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Timidly means in a shy and fearful manner.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Andrew hopes _______ (to move) to New York next year.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 'Hope' requires the Infinitive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The demand ___  labour is dependent on worker's productivity: the demand will be higher if he adds much to the revenue.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'demand for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It's sunny. Why are you carrying an umbrella? - Just __ case
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'in case'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: He is brilliant ___ public speaking.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'brilliant at something'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My little sister's favourite book is 'The Magic Swan- ___' (plural of a 'goose').
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The noun 'goose' has the irregular plural form: GOOSE - GEESE.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Did Rose buy ___ dress at the shopping centre yesterday? She has nothing to wear to the disco.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'any' in negative and interrogative sentences and 'some' in positive statements. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If Michael ___ (to become) an artist he ___ (can / to earn) a lot of money.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use Conditional 3 to express unreal conditions and results that could happen in the past: If-clause (if + Past Perfect) - Main Clause (would/could + perfect conditional or perfect continuous conditional). The meaning of this sentence: Michael was not a an artist so he didn't earn much money.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Find the correct word formation chain (noun - adjective - verb): authorization
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'authority - authoritarian - authorize'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Select the sentence with the right word order:
options: I certainly do like your idea! I'll dream up it.
I certainly do like your idea! I'll dream it up.

I certainly do like your idea! Up I'll dream it.

options_map.B: I certainly do like your idea! I'll dream it up.
options_map.C: I certainly do like your idea! I'll up dream it.
options_map.D: I certainly do like your idea! Up I'll dream it.

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The majority of transitive phrasal verbs are separable. Therefore, we can place the particle before the noun objects or after them. multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ____ Equator divides the globe into two hemispheres.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The is used before nouns which are unique.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Christopher ___ (to explore) the nature of our emotions in his new book. He also ___ (to give) detailed phsychological arguments to all conclusions.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Present Simple to talk about summaries and reviews.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: When Richard ___ (to come) in he ___ (to see) that Chasey (already / pack) a suitcase.

had come / had seen / had already packed

options_map.A: had come / saw / had already packed
options_map.D: had come / had seen / had already packed

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. We use the Past Simple for short completed actions in the past: came / saw. 2. We use the Past Perfect to show that one action happened before another one: first she had packed a suitcase and then he came in and saw it.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: By the time Chris ___ (to arrive) we ___ (to finish) watching the film.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Perfect to express the idea that one action will be completed before the second one in the future. Here: first we will stop watching the film and after that he will arrive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question:
Transfer this Active voice sentence to the Passive one: 
Carol was editing an important manuscript.

An important manuscript was  edited by Carol.
An important manuscript was being edited by Carol.

options_map.B: An important manuscript had been edited by Carol.
options_map.C: An important manuscript was  edited by Carol.
options_map.D: An important manuscript was being edited by Carol.
