multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The Past Continuous Passive is formed: [was / were + being + Past Participle].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It is important to ___ the first impression.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to make an impression'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The film was so tedious that Jerry ______ (to fall asleep accidentally) during it.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to nod off' means 'to fall asleep accidentally'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose two forms of the verb 'to dig' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO DIG - DUG - DUG.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: __________ that the opposition was strong, the ruling party managed to win the elections again.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'notwithstanding' to show contrast between parts of the sentence. We could also use here 'although, in spite of the fact that'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We all were sitting silently and waiting ___ for the news from the hospital.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Patiently means in a calm and quiet manner.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We planned ___ (to get) there by 6 p.m.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Plan requires the Infinitive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: A departure ____ normal blood pressure can cause many diseases.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'departure from'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Alex was sleeping ___ the lecture.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should use 'during' in the meaning of 'within a certain period'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Tyler looks very pale. It seems he's ill ____ fever or flu.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'ill with'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ water is wasted.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: In formal writing we use 'much or plenty of'. 'Many' is used with countable nouns.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It's late. If our neighbour ___ (not to turn) off the music in 5 minutes, I ___ (to call) the police.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about probable situations in the present or future we use Conditional 1: If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future/modal + present without 'to').

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Find the correct word formation chain (noun - adjective - verb): administration
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'administrator - administrative - administrate'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Determine the sentence with the right word order
options: Billy tried an extremely unusual and weird out gear.
Billy tried an extremely unusual and weird gear out.
Billy tried out an extremely unusual and weird gear.
Tried Billy out an extremely unusual and weird gear.

options_map.A: Billy tried an extremely unusual and weird out gear.
options_map.B: Billy tried an extremely unusual and weird gear out.
options_map.C: Billy tried out an extremely unusual and weird gear.
options_map.D: Tried Billy out an extremely unusual and weird gear.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Billy tried out an extremely unusual and weird gear.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The majority of transitive phrasal verbs are separable. Therefore, we can place the particle before the noun objects or after them. But we should remember that we place the particle after the verb if the noun is a part of a long and complicated phrase: tried out an extremely unusual and weird gear (CORRECT) / tried an extremely unusual and weird gear out (WRONG).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Mr. Rogers is one of ___ best engineers in our company.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'the' before superlative adjectives.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My family ___ (to have) supper now. But ___ (to have) a high temperature at the moment and I'm too weak to join them.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we talk about things in general, permanent situations and states or things that happen sometimes, we use the Present Simple Tense. When we describe an event that is happening in the moment of speaking we use the Present Continuous. Remember that some stative verbs (feel, have, see, seem, look, etc.) can be used in continuous form but with the change in meaning. Here: has - refers to possession / is having - means 'is eating'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: When I ___ (to enter) the room Mike ___ (to play) the guitar. He ___ (to play) all evening and ___ (to do) nothing about the house.
options: entered / was playing / was playing / had done
entered / was playing / had been playing / had done
entered / had been playing / had been playing / did

options_map.A: entered / was playing / was playing / had done
options_map.B: entered / was playing / had been playing / had done
options_map.C: entered / had been playing / had been playing / did

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: entered / was playing / had been playing / had done
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. We use the Past Simple for short completed actions in the past: entered the room. 2. We use the Past Continuous for interrupted actions which were in progress in the past - was playing the guitar. 3. We use the Past perfect Continuous to emphasize the duration of some action in the past - had been playing all evening. 4. We use here the Past Perfect to emphasize the result - had done nothing

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This time tomorrow I ________ (to cook) while Jim ________ (to clean) the car.
options: will be cooking / will be cleaning

options_map.A: will be cooking / will be cleaning

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: will be cooking / will be cleaning
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Continuous to emphasize that the action will be in progress in the future. Here the Future Continuous shows 2 simultaneous actions.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active voice sentence to the Passive one: When I was in Paris somebody stole jewelry and cash from my flat.
options: I was stolen jewelry and cash from my flat when I was in Paris.
Jewelry and cash were been stolen from my flat when I was in Paris.
Jewelry and cash were stolen from my flat when I was in Paris.
Jewelry and cash were being stolen from my flat when I was in Paris.

options_map.A: I was stolen jewelry and cash from my flat when I was in Paris.
options_map.B: Jewelry and cash were been stolen from my flat when I was in Paris.
options_map.C: Jewelry and cash were stolen from my flat when I was in Paris.
options_map.D: Jewelry and cash were being stolen from my flat when I was in Paris.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Jewelry and cash were stolen from my flat when I was in Paris.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The correct form of the Past Simple Passive is: [was / were + Past Participle].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The coach ___ us instructions.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'to give instructions'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Russel always supports me. He _______ (to support somebody) over my decision to move to London.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to back somebody up' means 'to support somebody'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Everybody loves Sarah. She is a _________  person who cares, always helps and makes your day sunny.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Kind-hearted means 'kind, gentle and showing sympathy'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: John was just ___ grateful that all his friends bothered to read his first book.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Pathetically means in a touching, moving and heartwarming manner.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Charles has finally finished ___ (to write) the report.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Finish requires the Gerund. In this case the Gerund is used as the object of the verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The results ___ this study were shocking.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'result of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jessica is only 6 but she has already learned a few poems ___ heart.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: By heart means 'to memorize by rot, word for word'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: He tends to be a leader who is worthy ___ respect and allegiance.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'worthy of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My doctor recommends me to limit consumption to three ______ a day.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Formally, 'coffee' is an uncountable noun and we cannot use it with '-s' ending. But there are some meanings when it is possible. For example, here: three coffees means '3 cups of coffee'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We left a glass of water on the windowsill for some days. Now ___ of water has evaporated.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'many, several and none' with countable nouns.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If Ann ___ (to wear) comfortable shoes, she ___ (not to hurt) her feet when hiking. (But she did in reality).
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use past unreal conditionals to refer to actions which never happened in reality. It can be an unreal result, imagined situation or regret about what really happened in the past. Here: in reality Ann hurt her feet because of uncomfortable shoes. Now she regrets about this.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Opt the sentence with the right word order
options: Joshua just do without fastfood and sweets cannot.
Joshua just cannot fastfood and sweets do without.
Joshua just cannot do fastfood and sweets without.
Joshua just cannot do without fastfood and sweets.

options_map.A: Joshua just do without fastfood and sweets cannot.
options_map.B: Joshua just cannot fastfood and sweets do without.
options_map.C: Joshua just cannot do fastfood and sweets without.
options_map.D: Joshua just cannot do without fastfood and sweets.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Joshua just cannot do without fastfood and sweets.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that there are separable and inseparable phrasal verbs. 'Do without' belongs to the group of phrasal verbs which cannot be devided.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Did you know that Rachel works for ___ Guardian (newspaper)?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We usually use the definite article before newspaper names.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jim  ___ (to work / usually) at the office but he ___ (to work) at home today.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. We use the Present Simple to talk about permanent and regular situations. 2. We use the Present Continuous to refer to temporary situations in the present.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The service company ___ (to apologise) because we ___ (to wait) for our car for 5 hours. We ___ (to be) totally exhausted.
options: apologised / had been waiting / had been

options_map.A: apologised / had been waiting / had been

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1,3. We use the Past Simple for short actions which were finished in the past. 2. We use the Past Perfect Continuous to emphasize the duration of the action which started in the past and continued up to some moment in the past.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: According to the schedule, we ___ (to depart) from London at 10 o'clock in the morning and ___ (to arrive) in Oslo at 3 p.m.  ___ (you / to meet) us?
options: will depart / will arrive / Are you meeting
will depart / will arrive / Will you meet

options_map.A: will depart / will arrive / Are you meeting
options_map.C: will depart / will arrive / Will you meet

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1,2. When we talk about scheduled events (planes, trains, etc.) we use the Present Simple. 3. When we make predictions or simple statements about the future we use the Future Simple.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Transfer this Active voice sentence to the Passive one: Sandra gave Mark an apple.
options: An apple was given to Sandra by Mark.
Sandra was given to Mark by an apple.
An apple was given to Mark by Sandra.
An apple had been given to Mark by Sandra.

options_map.A: An apple was given to Sandra by Mark.
options_map.B: Sandra was given to Mark by an apple.
options_map.C: An apple was given to Mark by Sandra.
options_map.D: An apple had been given to Mark by Sandra.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: An apple was given to Mark by Sandra.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Sometimes we need to change a sentence from the Active voice into the Passive voice. We can also know a person who carries out the action. In this case we form a sentence according to this word order:  Subject - Be+ Past Participle - Preposition 'BY' - Agent (who or what carries out the action). Here the Past Simple Passive should be used: was given. Other answers are illogical.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My Granny has always lived in the ___. She doesn't like big cities.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Countryside - is the area outside towns. 'Wildlife' determines some area where wild animals live, plants grow, etc.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jimmy ________ (to ask people the same question) but nobody told him how to get to the park.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to ask around' means 'to ask people the same question'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose two forms of the verb 'to beseech' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO BESEECH - BESOUGHT / BESEECHED - BESOUGHT / BESEECHED

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Vets tried hard to save my puppy. He died, _______ .
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'though' to express contrast between parts of the sentence. This linking word can be placed in the end of the statement while other words 'although, in spite of, despite, whereas, while' (they also express contrast) cannot. They are used to connect parts or in the very beginning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This cyclist seems to be ________ . He wins the sixth race this month.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Invincible means 'powerful, difficult to be defeated'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I'm not sure, but Jay is _______ in the park.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we are not sure about something we use the adverb 'probably'. Other adverbs represented in the answers express a high degree of certainty.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We prepared ________ (to get) up early in the morning.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Prepare requires the Infinitive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I don't understand you.  Give me at least one reason ___ your decision.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'reason for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Ella entered the room and smiled ___ Jose.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'smile at somebody'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My grandfather always told me to be faithful ___ the family and friends.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'faithful to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Most of all I like cars. I've got one. ___ is my greatest passion and hobby.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: On rare occasions we use  gendered pronouns to express our relation to some things very emotionally. We should remember that there are 3 genders in English: feminine, masculine and neutral. The word 'car' is of feminine gender.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I'm going to the supermarket to pick up food and drink. Is there ___ you need?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'something' to refer to things in affirmative sentences, while 'anything' in negative and interrogative ones. 'Everything' and 'nothing' do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express disappointment with the present situation: Garry has a cat allergy.
options: Garry wouldn't have had a cat allergy.
Garry wishes he hadn't had a cat allergy.
Garry wishes he didn't have a cat allergy.
Garry wouldn't have a cat allergy.

options_map.A: Garry wouldn't have had a cat allergy.
options_map.B: Garry wishes he hadn't had a cat allergy.
options_map.C: Garry wishes he didn't have a cat allergy.
options_map.D: Garry wouldn't have a cat allergy.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Garry wishes he didn't have a cat allergy.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To express disappointment with the present situation we usually use the construction 'I + wish + Past Simple'. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a prefix to make a word negative: rational
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'irrational - irrational'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Pick out the sentence with the right word order
options: Kate does rarely visit the gym.
Kate does visit the gym rarely.
Does rarely Kate visit the gym.
Rarely does Kate visit the gym.

options_map.A: Kate does rarely visit the gym.
options_map.B: Kate does visit the gym rarely.
options_map.C: Does rarely Kate visit the gym.
options_map.D: Rarely does Kate visit the gym.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Rarely does Kate visit the gym.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to speak in a more formal and literary way or we want to emphasize some idea in the sentence, we use the inversion. In this case the speaker wanted to point out the adverb 'rarely'. We put it in the first place. We place the auxiliary verb after the adverb 'rarely'. So the word order is: [adverb — auxiliary — subject — verb — object].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ Eiffel Tower is one of the most famous french attractions.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'the' before famous monuments, buildings, museums, etc.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: _______ (you / ever / to be) to Italy? We _______ (to go) there two years ago and still _______ (to remember) it.
options: Have you ever been / went / are remembering
Have you ever been / have gone / remember
Have you ever been / went / remember
Did you ever go / went / remember

options_map.A: Have you ever been / went / are remembering
options_map.B: Have you ever been / have gone / remember
options_map.C: Have you ever been / went / remember
options_map.D: Did you ever go / went / remember

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Have you ever been / went / remember
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. We use the Present Perfect to emphasise the result. Here: we do not know how many times you have visited Italy - from the past up to now. 2. We use the Past Simple to express what happened in the past - last summer, a day ago, yesterday, etc. 3. We use the Present Simple to refer to something regular.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Oh, I ___ (to see) an e-mail from the support service! They ___ (finally / to reply) me. I ___ (to wait) for it for 2 weeks.
options: see / have finally replied / have been waiting
am seeing / are finally replying / had been waiting

options_map.C: see / have finally replied / have been waiting
options_map.D: am seeing / are finally replying / had been waiting

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: see / have finally replied / have been waiting
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. When we use 'see' in the meaning of 'ability to see with our eyes' we use it in the form of the Present Simple. 2. When we see in the present the result of the action which started in the past and continued up to the certain moment in the present we use the Present Perfect tense. 3. We use the Present Perfect Continuous to emphasize the duration of the action which started in the past and continues up to the present.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: _______ (you / to come) to us to celebrate the date? We ________ (to be married) for 5 years on April 3rd.
options: Do you come / will have been married
Will you come / will be married
Will you come / will have been married
Will you come / are going to be married

options_map.A: Do you come / will have been married
options_map.B: Will you come / will be married
options_map.C: Will you come / will have been married
options_map.D: Will you come / are going to be married

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Will you come / will have been married
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1. When we make predictions or simple statements about the future we use the Future Simple. 2. We use the Future Perfect to talk about actions which will be completed in the future up to the certain time point: when the 3rd of April comes it would mean that 5 years have passed since their wedding.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Connect two sentences using the Passive voice: Thank you all for electing me as a leader of the team. It is a great honor for me.
options: Thank you all for have been electing me as a leader of the team and it is a great honor for me.
It is a great honor for me to be elected as a leader of the team.
It is a great honor for me that you have elected me as a leader of the team.
Electing as a leader of the team is a great honor for me.

options_map.A: Thank you all for have been electing me as a leader of the team and it is a great honor for me.
options_map.B: It is a great honor for me to be elected as a leader of the team.
options_map.C: It is a great honor for me that you have elected me as a leader of the team.
options_map.D: Electing as a leader of the team is a great honor for me.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: It is a great honor for me to be elected as a leader of the team.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Infinitive phrases in the passive voice help us construct sentences more gracefully and rationally. We create them: [to be + Past Participle]. They can take a position of the subject, object or modifier. Here it is on the place of the object.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Trisha was seasick on her first sea ___ across the Mediterranean.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Voyage - is a long trip, very often at sea. 'Journey' - means moving from one point to another in a vehicle (bus journey, train journey, etc.). Trip - covers the whole process (moving somewhere and back, rest, pleasure and purpose). 'Travel' - is used to talk about the activity of moving from one point to another generally (air travels has become more expensive this year).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The company ________ (to stop providing) the internet in our hotel. It's a great disappointment for us all.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Phrasal verb 'to cut off' means 'to stop providing'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose two forms of the verb 'to frostbite' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO FROSTBITE - FROSTBIT - FROSTBITTEN.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Animal rights groups have influenced on cosmetic companies greatly. ________ many brands have stopped testing products on animals.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'consequently' to talk about results and consequences. We could also use here 'so.. that, as a result, therefore'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Migrants to European countries often take ______ journeys over the sea. Sometimes they end up tragically.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Perilous means 'dangerous, unsafe, hazardous'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Tell me the reason ___ you didn't call me yesterday.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the relative adverbs to connect sentences. They also can replace a structure [preposition + which]. Here we choose 'why' because this answer is the most logically appropriate. We could also say 'for which' but this structure is more formal.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We postponed ___ (to return) to the town.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Return requires the Gerund. In this case the Gerund is used as the object of the verb.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The topic of today's lecture is an artistic description ___  the seasons in the works by A. Pushkin.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'description of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I'm so angry that my parents decided _______ buying a dog. I want it so much!
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we take a negative decision we 'decide against' something.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: All war veterans are worthy ___ respect.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'worthy of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Titanic has become one of the most famous ships in history, ____  memory kept alive by numerous books, folk songs, films, exhibits, and memorials.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: On rare occasions we use gendered pronouns to express our relation to some things very emotionally. We should remember that there are 3 genders in English: feminine, masculine and neutral. The word 'ship' is of feminine gender. Here we use the possessive form of the personal pronoun 'she'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My husband is always busy. He never does ___ chores.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'some' to refer to things in affirmative sentences, while 'any' in negative and interrogative ones.  'Nothing' and 'every' do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express disappointment with what somebody did in the past: Sandra moved to Paris a year ago.
options: If only Sandra moved to Paris a year ago.
I wish Sandra moved to Paris a year ago.
I'd rather Sandra didn't move to Paris a year ago.
I'd rather Sandra hadn't moved to Paris a year ago.

options_map.A: If only Sandra moved to Paris a year ago.
options_map.B: I wish Sandra moved to Paris a year ago.
options_map.C: I'd rather Sandra didn't move to Paris a year ago.
options_map.D: I'd rather Sandra hadn't moved to Paris a year ago.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: I'd rather Sandra hadn't moved to Paris a year ago.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we need to show disappointment with what somebody did in the past we often use a construction [would rather + subject + Past Perfect]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Form a compound adjective from two words: good + look:
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'good-looking'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Select the sentence with the right word order
options: I would tell him everything, were in your shoes I.
I were in your shoes, I would tell him everything.
Were I in your shoes, I would tell him everything.
I would tell him everything, I were in your shoes.

options_map.A: I would tell him everything, were in your shoes I.
options_map.B: I were in your shoes, I would tell him everything.
options_map.C: Were I in your shoes, I would tell him everything.
options_map.D: I would tell him everything, I were in your shoes.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: Were I in your shoes, I would tell him everything.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we invert the conditional sentence and omit 'if' we place 'should, were, had' in the first place: [should / were / had + subject + object] + [result clause].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ French make many delicious sorts of cheese.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the definite article to refer to a whole group of people.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Tom ___ (to make) phone calls to travel agencies all day long, but he ___ (still / not / to get) a suitable offer.
options: has been making / still doesn't get
has been making / still hasn't got

options_map.B: has been making / still doesn't get
options_map.D: has been making / still hasn't got

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: has been making / still hasn't got
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Present Perfect Continuous to emphasize the duration of the action which started in the past and continues up to now. We use the Present Perfect to emphasize the result - still hasn't found.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We ___ (to walk) in the park when the rain ___ (to start). There ___ (to be) no place to hide nearby. So we ___ (to get) cold that day.
options: were walking / had started / was / got
walked / were starting / was / had got
were walking / was starting / had been / got

options_map.A: were walking / had started / was / got
options_map.C: walked / were starting / was / had got
options_map.D: were walking / was starting / had been / got

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 1,2. To describe the situation when one action was in progress and the second one interrupted it we use two tenses: the Past Continuous for the longer action and the Past Simple for the shorter one. 3,4. We use the Past Simple to talk about short simple actions which were finished in the past.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ (you / to finish) working when I ___ (to come) to pick you up?
options: Will you have finished / will come

options_map.C: Will you have finished / will come

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation:
1. We use the Future Perfect to talk about actions which will be completed in the future up to the certain time point. 
2. When we make predictions or simple statements about the future we use the Future Simple.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Connect two sentences using the Passive voice: They blame me for something unfairly. It is very offensive.
options: I blamed by them for something unfairly and it is very offensive.
It is very offensive that they blame me for something unfairly.
To be blamed for something unfairly is very offensive.
Unfairly blamed for something is very offensive.

options_map.A: I blamed by them for something unfairly and it is very offensive.
options_map.B: It is very offensive that they blame me for something unfairly.
options_map.C: To be blamed for something unfairly is very offensive.
options_map.D: Unfairly blamed for something is very offensive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: To be blamed for something unfairly is very offensive.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Infinitive phrases in the passive voice help us construct sentences more gracefully and rationally. We create them: [to be + Past Participle]. multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The ______ can be cruel to the humanity. Devastating earthquakes or tsunamis can kill a lot of people.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to creep' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO CREEP - CREPT - CREPT.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Jogging gives you strength and health. ___, it makes you energetic and peppy.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'moreover' to introduce details to the information given above. We could also use here 'furthermore, what is more, also'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My friend likes travelling to nice ___ places which are unknown to the majority of tourists. He always takes there magnificent photos.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Quaint means 'curious, fanciful, elegant, unusual'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Danny still remembers the day ______ he first flew an aircraft.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'on which'. This structure is quite formal, so we could use here a relative adverb 'when'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We have arranged ___ (to meet) at 12 o'clock.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Arrange requires the Infinitive.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I didn't agree with Rachel's words. I took the objection ___ her remarks.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'objection to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We were disappointed ___  the hotel's service.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: 'disappointed with'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Britain is my Motherland. ___ will always be my favorite country in the world.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: On rare occasions we use  gendered pronouns to express our relation to some things very emotionally. multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Marion doesn't have ___ relatives in Italy.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'some' to refer to things in affirmative sentences, while 'any' in negative and interrogative ones.  'Nothing' and 'every' do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If  Sophia ______ (to become) a filmmaker, she  ______ (to shoot) documentary films.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about probable situations in the present or future we use Conditional 1: If-clause (if + Present Simple) - Main Clause (future/modal + present without 'to'). Here: Sophia is not a filmmaker yet, but she wishes to shoot films.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Find the correct word formation chain (noun - adjective - verb): aggravation
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'aggressor - aggravating - aggravate'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose the sentence with the right word order:

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: They ___ (to live) in that house for 3 years. They ___ (to move) to Denver about a year ago. But their house ___ (yet / not / to sell).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This time next month Elizabeth ___ (still / to work) in Spain.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use the Future Continuous to talk about unfinished actions which will be in progress in the future.

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we suppose or make a prediction we usually use the Passive Infinitives with the modal 'must'. Here we use the present perfect form of the Infinitive: [must] + [have + been + Past Participle].

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Smoking has a strong harmful ___  on our health.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation:
Affect - is a verb that means 'to change/make a difference'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Patrick is always ______ __ (to lie about something) stories about why he comes home late!

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose  two forms of the verb 'to bind' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO BIND - BOUND - BOUND

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Teachers should be friendly and loyal ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'as well' to add some positive information.

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Revengeful means 'resentful, a person who causes harm to anyone who hurts him'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a suffix to form a noun from a given word: disturb

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO FLING - FLUNG - FLUNG

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My sister chose a _______ pencil skirt and pale green top for her first date with Tom. She didn't want to look showy.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Clark ___ suggested that each member of the team should take the responsibility for results.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Andrew wasted time ___ (to play) games online all the day long.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The club succeeded ___ winning the championship.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Sammy could see ___ because of the rain. The road was becoming more and more dangerous.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'little' with verbs which are not followed by a noun.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express disappointment with the present situation: Paul wants to have a million dollars. But he hasn't got it.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Find the correct word formation chain (noun - adjective - verb): advice

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ as it may seem, he was awarded.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation:
'Amazing' is an adjective but 'amazingly' is an adverb. We say ' Amazing/lnteresting... as it may seem'.

The way to work this out is by changing the word order of the two alternatives as follows:
It may seem amazingly || It may seem amazing.
Obviously, 1 is incorrect — an adjective (describing ‘it’) is required, rather than an adverb. The latter could be used in a construction of the type:
Amazingly, he did exactly the opposite to what we had envisaged... or 'It was amazing that…' or 'We were amazed at…'
However that is style and personal preference, rather than grammar.

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO RIVE - RIVED - RIVEN / RIVED.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose two forms of the verb 'to wring' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO WRING - WRUNG - WRUNG.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose two forms of the verb 'to alight' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO ALIGHT - ALIT/ALIGHTED - ALIT/ALIGHTED.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Choose two forms of the verb 'to sting' according to the order: Past Simple - Past Participle
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: TO STING - STUNG - STUNG.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: We could phone Jill later, ___ we have to hurry up.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The meaning of this sentence is: we are in a hurry so we have no time to phone Jill. 'We have no time' is the reason why we cannot phone Jill. To give a reason for a certain situation we use 'seeing that, seeing as, as, because, since' + clause. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ the accident the flight was delayed.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The accident’ is the reason why the flight was delayed. To introduce a reason we could use owing to' and 'since', But you should remember that after 'since' we place a clause.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Carla was inattentive ___ she had a car accident.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we talk about a result we use 'so, therefore, as a result, for this reason'. Notice that they are usually come at the beginning of the sentence but it is possible for 'so' and 'therefore' to take also a middle position. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ the	weather forecasts the city was hit by huge snowstorm.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we want to show there is a surprising contrast between two statements in one sentence we use 'although, though, even though' and 'despite/in spite of + -ing/noun/pronoun'. Other given linking words do not relate to the meaning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Our boss announced that ___ those employees who came late for work would have their salary deducted accordingly.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Henceforth means 'from this time on'. We use this linking word to introduce a new idea that differs from something that was ordinary and habitual before.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: These two vases look rather similar, ___ they are the same shape and color.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 'Inasmuch as' is used to add a comment with more details, explain something more clearly.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ that the opposition was strong, the ruling party managed to win the elections again.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'notwithstanding' to show contrast between parts of the sentence. We could also use here 'although, in spite of the fact that'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Miners went on strike ___ bad working conditions.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'on account of' to give reasons and describe the cause. 'Bad working conditions’ is the cause why miners went on strike.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Vets tried hard to save my puppy. He died, ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'though' to express contrast between parts of the sentence. This Linking word can be placed in the end of the statement while other words 'although, in spite of, despite, whereas, while' (they also express contrast) cannot. They are used to connect parts or in the very beginning of the sentence.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This green sofa is ___ (cozy) than the yellow one.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we compare two things or two people we use the comparative form of adjectives. We add [-er / -ier] to short adjectives.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Homer describes the ___ customs of the Greeks in his poem 'The Odyssey'.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: 'Immemorial' means 'ancient'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My friend Likes travelling to nice ___ places which are unknown to the majority of tourists. He always takes there magnificent photos.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Quaint means 'curious, fanciful, elegant, unusual’.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ speaking, this song	is utter garbage.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to use the adverv 'bluntly'. It means 'direct manner of speaking'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This politician is not a person who speaks ___ about the real economic situation in the country.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The adverb 'truthfully' means that someone speaks honestly.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The vase was very fragile. Garry placed it down on the table ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Gingerly means 'carefully'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Danny still remembers the day ___ he first flew an aircraft.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'on which'. This structure is quite formal, so we could use here a relative adverb 'when'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The king fall heir ___ his daughter.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'to fall heir to'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I have a recipe ___ paella with seafood. I can give it to you.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'recipe for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Do you know that water pollution is one of offences ___ the environment and that it is punished by law?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'offence against'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The store announced a huge decrease ___ prices.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'decrease in'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The demand ___ labour is dependent on worker’s productivity: the demand will be higher if he adds much to the revenue.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions with them: 'demand for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: A departure ___ normal blood pressure can cause many diseases.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions with them: 'departure from'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I don't understand you. Give me at least one reason ___ your decision.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions with them: 'reason for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Our boss took credit ___ the work our department did.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use preposition ’for’ after the noun 'credit' in the idiom: 'to take credit for'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The newspaper's report ___ choosing the most convenient place for living was not well researched.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions with them: 'research on'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ avoidance of misunderstanding you should check the information attentively.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'in avoidance of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: The figure skating competition is ___ now.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'to be underway'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Mary is still in the hospital. But she is ___ high spirits.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'in high spirits'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Look! The helicopter is flying ___ us.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'to fly over something/somebody'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Ben is going to travel ___ China from May ___ July.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'through China' and 'from May through July’.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ times he can behave with insolence.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'at times'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My brother rejoiced ___ hearing the news.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say 'rejoice at something'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Robert excels ___ playing lawn tennis.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: It is correct to say ’excel at'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This plateau is rich ___ different minerals.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: ’rich in’.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Never be jealous ___ someone’s success. You never know it's price.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some adjectives are used with specific prepositions after them: ’jealous of'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Unfortunately, hunters kill many ___ every year.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are some nouns which have the same form in the singular and in the plural: ONE GROUSE - TWO GROUSE.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I think we should move our ___ (a ski) to garage.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: The right plural form of the noun 'ski' is 'skis'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Some peculiarities of the language should be noted in ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are many nouns which have Greek or Latin origin. As a rule, they keep own endings: ONE PARENTHESIS - TWO PARENTHESES.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Scientists say that stars called supergiants have ___ (a radius) many times larger than that of our planet.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are many nouns which have Greek or Latin origin. As a rule, we memorise their forms: A RADIUS - TWO RADII. 'Radiuses' also can be used.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: They watched the performance through ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation:
Some nouns are always plural: SCISSORS/GLASSES/
TROUSERS/JEANS/
SHORTS/TIGHTS/
PYGAMAS/NEWS/
BINOCULARS etc.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My little niece likes ___ very much.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are some nouns which have the same form in the singular and in the plural: FRUIT - FRUIT (if we speak about it in general). But speaking about different types - we say: KINDS OF FRUITS.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Bus is a very comfortable ___ of transport.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: There are some nouns which have the same form in the singular and in the plural: ONE MEANS - TWO MEANS.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: My doctor recommends me to Limit consumption to three ___ a	day.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Formally, 'coffee' is an uncountable noun and we cannot use it with '-s ending. But there are some meanings when it is possible. For example, here three coffees means '3 cups of coffee'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: It’s too dark in the room, I can hardly see ___ here.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'any / anything' in negative sentences and in positive sentences with 'never, hardly, without’.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Would you Like an apple or a banana? - It doesn't matter, ___ is good for me.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Either is used to express a similarity with a statement made. Here: you can give an apple or a banana because I like them both.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Formal writing: ___ water is wasted.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: In formal writing we use 'much or plenty of. 'Many' is used with countable nouns.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Sammy could see ___ because	of the rain. The road was becoming more and more dangerous.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We use 'little' with verbs which are not followed by a noun.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express the idea when you want someone to do something in the present or future: It’s late. Don't go there alone.
options: If only you hadn't gone there alone.
I wish you hadn't gone there alone.
I'd rather you went there alone.
I'd rather you didn't go there alone.

options_map.C: I'd rather you went there alone.
options_map.D: I'd rather you didn't go there alone.

multiple_choice_quizzes.correct_text: I'd rather you didn't go there alone.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we need to express the idea when you want someone to do something in the present or future we usually use the construction [would rather + subject + Past Simple]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Express disappointment with the present situation: I want to be popular. But I'm not.
options: If only I had been popular when I wanted.
If I were popular I would want it.
I would be popular if I wanted.

options_map.B: If I were popular I would want it.
options_map.C: I would be popular if I wanted.

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: To express disappointment with the present situation we usually use the construction [ I + wish + Past Simple]. Other answers do not relate to the meaning.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: If Mike ___ (to have) time he ___ (can earn) more teaching Polish in addition to his main work.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When we speak about imaginary situations which differ from real facts in the present we use Conditional 2: If-clause (if + Past Simple) - Main Clause (would/could + present without 'to'). The meaning of this sentence: in reality Mike doesn't have enough time to earn additional money.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a suffix to form an adjective from a given word: baby
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say 'babyish'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Use a suffix to form an adjective from a given word: sympathy
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We say ’sympathetic.

options: I lie in bed at night, thinking about dinosaurs.

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation:
Lie is an intransitive verb and doesn’t require an object. It means to rest in a horizontal position or to be located somewhere. (LIE - LAY - LAIN)
Lay is a transitive verb and will be followed by a direct object. It means to put something or someone down (often in a horizontal position). (LAY - LAID - LAID)
Lie also means to say something that isn't true but it's a regular verb and it takes the following form (LIE / LIED / LIED - Lying).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: “Prepare ___ jump”, he said.

Prepare for + noun (where “for” is a preposition).
Prepare to + verb (where “to” is an infinitive marker).

Passive of this:

I think he will not pass.

options_map.B: I think he will not pass.

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: When negative ideas are introduced in a noun clause with the following verbs in principal clause, it is advisable to make principal clause in negative.

You are requested kindly to stay for sometime.

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Spilt in definitive, 'to' should not be separated from its verb by inserting any adverb between to two: I advised him to carry carefully the bag.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Which one is correct:
options: What do you suggest us to do.
What do you suggest we should do.

options_map.B: What do you suggest we should do.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question:
Active: do not insult him

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: His written ​French is very good but he ​needs to practise ​___ it.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation:
We say practise + gerund:
His written ​French is very good but he ​needs to practise ​speaking it.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: There's nothing you can do about the situation, so ___ worrying about it.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation:
It's no good/it's no use + -ing(gerund):
There is nothing you can do about the situation, so it's no use worrying about it.
It's no good trying to persuade me. You won't suceed.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: ___ working hard you would have failed. (except for)
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation:
But for + gerund/noun: if it were not for someone or something.
But for working hard you would have failed.
But for the children, Mrs. Smith would have left her husband years ago.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Congratulation / (s)?
options: Congratulations! You must be feeling very proud.
Congratulation! You must be feeling very proud.

options_map.A: Congratulations! You must be feeling very proud.
options_map.B: Congratulation! You must be feeling very proud.

multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Congratulations is a plural noun: 'Many congratulations to you both. I'm sure you'll be very happy together.' 'Give them our congratulations and say that we'll be getting in touch soon.'

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Protect me ___ what I want.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: We should remember that some nouns are used with specific prepositions after them: 'protect from'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: This is a ___ event.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation:
The adjective 'historic' means 'having importance in history' or 'having influence on history'.
The adjective 'historical' means 'having taken place in history', 'from the past' or 'pertaining to history'.
This is a historical event. (one that happened in the past).
This is a historic event. (one that is important in history, e.g., the Moon landing).

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I ordered personalized ___.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Stationery is writing and office supplies. The most common error associated with this pairing is writing 'stationary' instead of 'stationery'.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: I took control of a large ___ of money.
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation:
Singular noun and can be measured or counted => 'quantity'.
'Amount' is for uncountables and 'number of' is for plural nouns.

multiple_choice_quizzes.question: Plural of addendum?
multiple_choice_quizzes.explanation: Addendum: [n]appendix, postscipt.
